## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=62, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation and maintenance of public disclosure standards for determining Company Confidential Information (CCI) (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public disclosures (i.e., data and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the process for collecting, compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=185, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure of clinical study information (including product information).

- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.

- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, word) in any format/medium whether it is directly entered into a database or provided in a document. |
| Disclosing Party | Astellas employees and non-employees who will disclose information publicly. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but are not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing application modules, manuscripts, scientific publications, abstracts or presentations. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (i.e., data and/or document) of clinical study information (including product information) in the public domain. |
| Public domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public, and therefore not subject to copyright.  Refer to the OVERVIEW Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

---

## SECTION 5: OVERVIEW

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=198, tables=1)_

- Disclosure of clinical study information as well as product information in clinical studies has increased in recent years due to implementation of disclosure regulations.

- The data and documents that must be disclosed by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following, due to these regulations:

- Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released, could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. Astellas commits to following these disclosure regulations and ensuring the protection and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain. Public domains in which Astellasâ€™ information are disclosed include, but are not limited to, the following:

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, regulations and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards may evolve and will be updated when necessary.

- Furthermore, FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library, will be used as the basis for Asset-specific classification and described in this procedure.

**Table 1 (overview_table_1):**

| Phase 1-4 |
| --- |
| ClinicaTrials.gov / CTIS (EU CTR) / EU Clinical Trials Register (EU Directive, via EudraCT) / Japan jRCT / National/country specific registries / Company website (e.g., Astellas Clinical Trials) / Third-party website (e.g., TrialSummaries.com hosted by TrialScope) / Scientific journal websites/databases / Materials presented during scientific events and conferences |
| Phase 4 Additional Databases |
| HMA-EMA Catalogues of RWD studies (Non-interventional studies) / Health Authorities clinical data public websites/databases / Ad-hoc requests for Astellas documents submitted to EMA (Policy 0043) |

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=109, tables=1)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is classified and disclosed in a consistent manner. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that May Be Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert, Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department, for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that May Be Considered CCI / <Throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development.> | Information Not Considered CCI / <Information relating to the nonclinical and clinical development of the medicinal product is not, per se, commercially confidential.> |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: if the manufacturing method of the active ingredient can be inferred through publication of such information / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / Tests conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special test and test methods: special test animal species or strains, test methods, rationale for setting tests, etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on test methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic tests / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The test methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of solvents used in studies / Nonclinical study results / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |
| Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) | Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) |
| Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) | All other information included in RMP is considered disclosable |

## SECTION 2: public disclosure Project | Project Background

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_project_background_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: Public Disclosure Project Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 2_

_Signals: medium (words=193, tables=0)_

- 2

- Process Benchmarking & Internal Interviews (led by Data Science Team)

- To assess public disclosure awareness, gaps, challenges and recommendations
- To assess the need for a centralized group for the maintenance of standards and tracking of public disclosures

- 41 interviews conducted with various functional representatives
- Groups Interviewed:

- Purpose

- Approach

- Outputs

- Lack of public disclosure standards
- Lack of clarity of owner of the data and the decision maker
- Lack of visibility of public disclosure outside of Astellas
- Missing standard approach for collecting, monitoring and maintaining for Data Disclosure Regulatory Intelligence

- M&D LT Endorsement

- Identify and develop public disclosure strategy, standards and centralized activities
- To include maintenance of standards for phases of development (phase 0 â€“ 4)
- Centralization of public disclosure tracking outside of Astellas
- Centralization of tracking for public disclosure regulatory intelligence
- Establishment of a Public Disclosure Group (expansion of scope of current Clinical Transparency Group, that sits within Data Science)

- May-Jul 2023

- Oct 2023

- Clinical Operations
- Legal
- Data Science
- Manufacturing & Technology
- Pharmacovigilance
- Medical Affairs
- Regulatory Affairs
- Early Development (Clin Ops and Clinical Pharmacology Science)
- Primary Focus Development Divisions (Asset Lead - BioPharma and Oncology, PF Development Division Heads)
- Business Development (Alliance Management)

## SECTION 3: public disclosure Project | Executive Summary

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_executive_summary_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: Public Disclosure Project Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 3_

_Signals: medium (words=240, tables=0)_

- Lack of centralized standards, oversight, and accountability for compliance with global regulations leads to inconsistent public disclosure.
- Public disclosure activities are decentralized and managed independently by M&D Functional Units
- There is no single point of contact or decision-maker responsible for developing cohesive standards/best practices and accountable for ensuring organizational compliance with global regulations
- There is no mechanism currently to centrally track what is disclosed in the public domain

- OBJECTIVE

- Ensure centralized standards, tracking and regulatory intelligence for public disclosure in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, industry guidance, as well as Astellas policies related to public disclosure in the public domain.

- 3

- If Astellas does not execute the project:
- Increased risk of inconsistency in public disclosures shared in public domain
- Potential exposure CCI impacting competitive edge
- Duplicative efforts by different divisions for identification of already disclosed information in public domains

- Start Date: March 2024
- Target End Date: Q3 FY24

- SCOPE OF WORK

- Develop a public disclosure strategy for data and document deliverables that includes the following components:
- Establish Astellas Global Public Disclosure Strategic Plan that includes public disclosure standards
- Centralize tracking of public disclosures shared in public domain
- Centralize disclosure regulatory intelligence/requirements (repository)
- Form a dedicated internal group that establishes Astellasâ€™ position on public disclosure and handles all deviations from standards
- NOTE: The scope will be limited to public disclosures pertaining to M&D. The scope may broaden in the future to encompass additional organizational groups within Astellas.

- PROBLEM STATEMENT

- RISKS

- TIMELINE

## SECTION 4: public disclosure Project | what problem are we solving?

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_what_problem_are_we_solving_

_Layout: Slide with two cloumns_

_Source: Public Disclosure Project Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 4_

_Signals: medium (words=143, tables=0)_

- 4

- ISSUE

- IMPACT

- SOLUTION

- Inefficient engagement & Potential loss of credibility

- Inefficient use of time and resources

- Redundant efforts & potential delays in the submission process

- Redaction request submitted for information already unredacted in a previous EU CTIS protocol amendment submission.

- Request from Astellas to redact information rejected by Health Canada due to information already in the public domain.

- Teams are manually searching Google for publicly available disclosures instead of using internal resources.

- Public Disclosure
- Strategic Plan
- Company position
- Global Public Disclosure standards & processes
- New Public Disclosure Group

- Public Disclosure
- Tracking Solution
- Centralized Public Disclosure tracking
- Defined Public Disclosure metrics and tracking requirements
- Public Disclosure tracking processes

- CCI Asset-specific Library
- Resource tool for asset leads/teams and functional teams to use to identify CCI
- Streamlined access to information with defined list of CCI for each asset
- Consistent process for public disclosure of information

## SECTION 5: public disclosure Project | Business Value

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_business_value_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: Public Disclosure Project Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 5_

_Signals: medium (words=135, tables=0)_

- 5

- Consistency and Structure
- Public disclosure standards will establish a consistent framework for sharing information publicly throughout the drug development lifecycle for Astellas products, thereby reducing the risk of impacting our competitive edge.
- Enhanced Decision-making
- Clear guidelines on what constitutes CCI, empowering asset teams to make informed decisions about what can be shared publicly.
- Efficient Review Processes
- Using CCI Asset Library and the tracking tool as the resource to support decision-making will lead to remove duplication efforts in identification of already public information, reduced review time, reduced need for ad-hoc decisions and deviations from defined standards.
- Centralized and Supportive Infrastructure
- Establishment of the â€˜Public Disclosure Groupâ€™ will provide dedicated administrative support, allowing asset leads and teams to concentrate on sharing the required information needed to create robust CCI Asset-specific Libraries that reflect the defined standards.

- I. PURPOSE
- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation
- and maintenance of public disclosure standards for determining Company Confidential
- Information (CCI) (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public
- disclosures (i.e., data and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the
- process for collecting, compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.
- II. SCOPE
- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to
- public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and
- the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas
- information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public
- disclosure of clinical study information (including product information).
- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.
- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide
- for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.
- The following organizations are in scope of this document:
- â€¢ Alliance Management
- â€¢ Clinical Operations
- â€¢ Communications & Investor Relations
- â€¢ Data Science
- Printed/downloaded documents must be verified to ensure use of official current version.
- ASTELLAS CONFIDENTIAL AND PROPRIETARY Page 1 of 8

- IV. OVERVIEW
- Disclosure of clinical study information as well as product information in clinical studies has
- increased in recent years due to implementation of disclosure regulations.
- The data and documents that must be disclosed by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing
- Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following, due to these regulations:
- â€¢ Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released,
- could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and
- financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,
- and/or
- â€¢ Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected
- personal data (PPD)).
- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. Astellas commits to

- public disclosures in the public domain. Public domains in which Astellasâ€™ information are

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=60, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation and maintenance of standards for determining Company Confidential Information (CCI) (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public disclosures (i.e., data and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the process for collecting, compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=185, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure of clinical study information (including product information).

- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.

- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

---

| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, ) in any format/medium. |
|   |   |
| Disclosing Party | Astellas employees and non-employees who disclose information publicly. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing application modules, manuscripts, scientific publications, abstracts or presentations. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (i.e., data and/or document) clinical study information (including product information)  public domain. |
| Public domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public, and therefore not subject to copyright.  Refer to the OVERVIEW Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public.  the protection and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain. Public domains in which Astellasâ€™ information are disclosed include, but are not limited to, the following:

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards evolve and will be updated when necessary.

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=109, tables=1)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is classified and disclosed in a consistent manner. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that May Be Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert, Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=84, tables=0)_

- This GL applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This GL applies to Astellas information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure of clinical study information (including product information).

- This GL is a companion document of SOP-AST-XXXXX Creation and Maintenance of CCI Public Disclosure Standards and Public Disclosure Tracking.

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that May Be Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: if the manufacturing method of the active ingredient can be inferred through publication of such information / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special and methods: special test animal species or strains, methods, rationale for setting , etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of solvents used in studies / Nonclinical study results / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |
| Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) | Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) |
| Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) | All other information included in RMP is considered disclosable |

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation and maintenance of standards for determining Company Confidential Information (CCI) (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public disclosures (i.e., data and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the process for collecting, compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure_SME comments.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=185, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure of clinical study information (including product information).

- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.

- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure_SME comments.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, ) in any format/medium. |
|   |   |
| Disclosing Party | Astellas employees and non-employees who disclose information publicly. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing application modules, manuscripts, scientific publications, abstracts or presentations. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (i.e., data and/or document) clinical study information (including product information)  public domain. |
| Public domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public, and therefore not subject to copyright.  Refer to the OVERVIEW Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-XXXXX CCI Public Disclosure_SME comments.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=109, tables=1)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is classified and disclosed in a consistent manner. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that May Be Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert, Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-XXXXX CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-XXXX CCI Public Disclosure Standards_SME Comments.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that May Be Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: if the manufacturing method of the active ingredient can be inferred through publication of such information / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special and methods: special test animal species or strains, methods, rationale for setting , etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of solvents used in studies / Nonclinical study results / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |
| Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) | Pharmacovigilance Related Information (Risk Management Plan) |
| Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) | All other information included in RMP is considered disclosable |

These cannot be CCI as they need to be disclosed via CTIS and via clinicaltrials.gov | RA | No Changes Made | It is a standard that endpoints that do not support the label are considered exploratory and are not subject to disclosure. |   |   |
| GUIDE-AST-XXX | IV |   | PW | RA | I very much miss in the table the perspective of when information would be disclosed during development. This is only mentions in general at the table heading, but this plays such an important role that the way the table is set does not work in my opinion. E.g. all information included in the RMP is considered disclosable. But that is of course only after the product has been approved and not earlier. The same applies to many other bullets | RA | No Changes Made | It is difficult to be overly prescriptive for all phases as there are various scenarios that will use this guide.  Reflecting the different stages of development in the Standards, would not be possible for standards due to the nature of each Primary focus. This approach was endorsed by the asset leads and they agreed that they would use these standards and they would apply the standards for each phase using the Asset-specific library. Per the introduction text, CCI standards apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval. Information relating to the nonclinical and clinical development of the asset is not, per se, commercially confidential. |   |   |
| SOP-AST-XXXX | I |   | RCW | RA | The purpose does not describe that this SOP describes the dpreparation of the CCI Asset-Specific Library Form. | RA | No Changes Made | We do not want to call out this process specifically in the purpose. Note that this is captured within the statement "describe the process for creation and maintenance" |   |   |
| SOP-AST-XXXX | II |   | PW | RA | Also here I struggle with the scope. Who will now be trained on this SOP? | RA | No Changes Made | The intention is that all of these organizations are going to receive a notification via LMS Training to further determine who within their organization should be trained (i.e. either for awareness or active responsibility) |   |   |
| SOP-AST-XXXX | IV |   | PW | RA | The sentence that starts with "Astellas commits to â€¦."should be removed form this SOP. That is not language that belongs in an SOP And in addition, why should Astellas commit to something when they are writing their own procedures | RA | No Changes Made | Updated statement to: This procedure will be used to ensure the protection of CCI and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain |   |   |
| SOP-AST-XXXX | IV |   | PW | RA | The text mentions that the public domains mentioned in the table include but are not limited to the following. That makes it difficult to understand what is seen as public disclosure as also in the scope section reference it made to this section | RA | No Changes Made | As noted in our meeting, this will be a phased approach and the table may not be exhaustive at this time. By adding the language of "but are not limited to" allows us to add more public domains in scope without having to update the SOP right away. |   |   |
| SOP-AST-XXXX | IV |   | PW | RA | It is true that disclosure of clinical study information and product information has increased but that is not the reason for this procedure. We should just mention that there are legal obligations to disclose information on our products. This SOPs intention is not to determine what is to be disclosed or not as that is a function perspective/decision. The Guide is considered standards for consistency; however, the ultimate determination is by the function per asset. |   |   |

- Disclosure Overview

- The purpose of this document is to support the anonymization of personal information (also called protected personal data [PPD] or protected personal information [PPI]) and commercially confidential information (CCI or also called [CBI] â€“ confidential business information) in documents intended for public disclosure. Anonymization of patient/subject/participant identifying information from internal Astellas documents is managed as per SOP-1691 Subject Identifying Information Management and is out of scope of this document.

- This document focuses on the simplest anonymization technique called masking - removal of values for variables which allow direct or indirect identification of an individual from the information. Masking can be achieved by using a redaction tool (available in Adobe or other application) which ensures that the redacted information is irreversibly blocked out. Masking of pre-specified variables can be performed manually and/or may include the use of software. This document covers the instructions when documents are redacted manually. Other anonymization techniques based on the quantitative risk assessments using a pre-specified threshold or other qualitative risk assessments are not covered in this document. If a document such as clinical study report or integrated summaries of more than one study requires the application of any other anonymization method, this may be achieved by applying a validated software to measure risk and anonymize the clinical documents.

- As global requirements for disclosure increase, where possible, only one version of a disclosure document should appear in the public space.

- Overall Redacted Document Flow

- Determining Personal Protected Data and Company Confidential Information

- Personal Protected Data

- Each Health Authority has a slightly different definition of personal information. See Reference section for links to Health Authority websites where exact definitions can be located.

- The European Medicines Agency (EMA) definition which is generally accepted globally is described here, which is aligned with the definition of Personal Information under Astellas Global Data Privacy Policy POL-412. Personal protected data is defined as any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ('data subject'); an identifiable person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identification number or to one or more factors specific to their physical, physiological, mental, economic, cultural or social identity. Refer to Appendix 1 for categories of personal information redacted in Astellas documents. Adjustments may need to be made for local national privacy laws and regulations.

- Documents created using â€œdisclosure readyâ€ templates may not require PPD redactions; however, documents will still be reviewed and finalized as described in SOP-AST-10344 Development of Disclosure Documents for Public Databases and Publications.

- Company Confidential Information

- Each Health Authority may have different criteria for defining a company confidential information (CCI).

- CCI is defined by EMA as â€œinformation contained in clinical documents that is not in the public domain or publicly available and where disclosure may undermine the legitimate economic interest of the company.â€ Health Canada has additionally added that the person (Astellas) has taken measures that are reasonable to ensure that the information remains unavailable to the public. Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) defines instructions for redaction requirements using the six categories of information found in the documents for public disclosure. Refer to Reference section for links to Health Authority Websites where the description of what information qualifies as CCI can be located.

- Points to consider prior to proposing redactions for CCI. If the piece of information meets any of the below criteria, generally, it will not be considered a CCI and not accepted by Health Authorities as such if proposed for redaction:

- Information already available in the public domain concerning the productâ€™s development should not be proposed for redaction (e.g. available publication of clinical information by Health Authorities, study design, development plan timelines and results):

- Sponsors, applicantsâ€™/MAHsâ€™ own website (Astellas website or the business/co-development partner website).

- Clinical trials registries (such as EU Clinical Trials Register, ClinicalTrials.gov).

- Health Authority websites (e.g., EMA, FDA, PMDA, TGA, Health Canada).

- Especially when the product (or another product containing the same active substance) is approved in one of these jurisdictions

- Public reports on the product, including but not limited to Public Assessment Report (EMA), Review Reports (PMDA) or Approval Package Review Reports (FDA)

- Patent databases

- Scientific literature and articles (such as medical journals, PubMed, Medline)

- Scientific knowledge and advancements within the relevant (for the product) therapeutic area(s):

- Confirm that the information is not available in the public domain

- Confirm whether the piece of information is innovative and whether its release could undermine the economic interests or competitive position of Astellas.

- If the piece of information is not innovative but it is still considered by Astellas that its disclosure may undermine the economic interest or competitive position of Astellas, then that piece of information can be considered CCI

- Examples of the information that may be considered a CCI includes:

- The excipients quantitative composition of the investigational/authorised product

- The site and names of manufacturers or suppliers of the active substance and drug product, including non-Astellas products or the excipients

- Suppliersâ€™ information (e.g., CTM) if disclosure is restricted and not permitted by contractual agreements

- Information related to future development plans for indications other than the one under investigation and not yet disclosed in the public domain

- In general, nonclinical and clinical data is not considered confidential information.

- CCIs are identified by the review team; however, the team should consider a global perspective and all the applicable regions that a redacted document will be required and follow a consistent decision-making process.

- Documents created using â€œdisclosure readyâ€ templates may not require CCI redactions, however, documents will still be reviewed and finalized as described in SOP-AST-10344.

- Redaction specifications

- Each Health Authority may have different required redaction specifications. As a general principle, Astellas documents are redacted using the EMA specifications. It is recommended to confirm this approach with the Clinical Transparency Lead for study registry /disclosure of study results or Regulatory Affairs Lead for marketing authorization submissions intended for publishing by more than one Health Authority.

- EMA Redaction Specifications

- EMA has explicit specifications for redaction as shown below. These can be set in the redaction properties in Adobe.

- Health Canada Redaction Specifications

- Health Canada does not have color specifications for redaction. The redaction overlay terms are Protected Personal Information (PPI) and Confidential Business Information (CBI). Health Canada will accept redactions using the EU specifications.

- PMDA Redaction Specifications

- PMDA does not have specific recommendations for redaction but typically accept black box redactions.

- How to Propose and Apply Redactions

- Adobe Recommendations

- In the Adobe tools menu open the redaction menu. Add the â€œMark for Redactionâ€ and â€œApplyâ€ buttons to the quick toolbar by drag and drop. This will allow redactions to be proposed and applied without having to open the entire redaction menu every time.

- It is also recommended to open the Edit PDF menu and drag and drop the button to â€œAdd Text.â€ This allows text boxes to be added when needed without the need to open the edit menu each time.

- Proposing Redactions with Adobe

- Open the PDF that requires redaction and click on the â€œMark for Redaction button as highlighted below, chose â€œText & Images.â€

- See section 3.1 for the EMA redaction specifications used for all Astellas documents at this time. Hover over the text, click and hold while dragging across the text to propose redaction. See the examples below. The proposed redaction will show as an outline around the text while it is in review and proposed redactions can be deleted, moved, or changed while applied redactions cannot be modified.

- Applying Redactions

- Open the PDF that is ready for redactions to be applied and click on the â€œApplyâ€ button.

- A pop up box will appear asking if you would like to continue. This operation cannot be undone and a new document will need to be started if redactions need to be modified after they have been applied. Click â€œOKâ€ to continue.

- A pop up window should appear saying the redactions have been successfully applied and asking if hidden information should be removed. Click â€œYes.â€

- Adobe will search the document for hidden information and the results will pop up in a column on the left of the document. Click â€œRemove.â€

- A pop up will appear for confirmation to continue. Click â€œOK.â€

- Adobe will run and a status update will appear in the left column when complete â€œRemoving selected itemsâ€¦ Done.â€ The document is ready to be saved and uploaded to Electronic Document Management System (EDMS).

- Removing Signature Page

- In Adobe tools menu, open the Organize Pages menu. Click on the signature page (it should be the last page in the document) that you want to remove. Then, go back to the toolbar menu. Check â€œDelete Pages after extractingâ€ box and click on â€œExtractâ€ to complete the task, as shown on the screenshot below.

- Close the extracted page and click â€œYesâ€ to save the change to the file from which the page was extracted.

- Adding NCT# to Protocol and SAP Cover Page

- The ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT#) is added to the cover page of the most current protocol and SAP that are prepared for public disclosure.

- To add the NCT#, click on the add text button (see adobe recommendations section). A pop-up window to format the text box will appear.

- Use your cursor to place the text box after the EudraCT#/EU Clinical Trial # or IND # mid page. Type in the NCT#, highlight and choose to turn the text blue.

- Black Box Redactions

- Redactions were originally performed with black boxes as shown below. Some regional Health Authorities may still request black box redactions however generally the EMA specifications are utilized. Documents with black box redactions were not revised when new redaction specifications were adopted. These documents will remain and be utilized as needed unless required by a Health Authority where the black boxes do not meet specifications any longer, in which case, they will be revised to meet the current redaction specifications and will not need to be reapproved.

- Black box redactions are the â€œout of the boxâ€ setting for redaction in Adobe. If this is required, reset redaction properties in Adobe to Black for â€œredacted area fill colorâ€ and delete overlay text.

- reference

- EMA Clinical Trial Regulation: Transparency rules: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory/research-development/clinical-trials/clinical-trials-regulation#transparency-rules-section

- EMA/90915/2018: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/regulatory-procedural-guideline/external-guidance-implementation-european-medicines-agency-policy-publication-clinical-data_en-3.pdf

- Health Canada Public Release of Clinical Information: guidance document: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drug-health-product-review-approval/profile-public-release-clinical-information-guidance/document.html

- Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario. De-identification Guidelines for Structured Data. June 2016. Available from: https://www.ipc.on.ca/wpcontent/ uploads/2016/08/Deidentification-Guidelines-for-Structured-Data.pdf
