| Astellas staff / including members of IDMC/SDAC | User ID. / Personal/staff information: name (except for the CSR signatories noted in the â€˜Retainâ€™ column), initials, email, phone number and signature, academic (e.g., Professor) or organizational (e.g., VP of Oncology Research) titles, or job titles. | Study roles (e.g., Statistician) / Clinical Study Report (CSR): Names of the sponsorâ€™s and coordinating investigator (CI) signatories of the CSR / Academic Qualifications (e.g., MD). / References to the sponsor company. / Sponsor company contact information and addresses. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=62, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define the process for the development, review and approval of all publications generated by an Astellas employee or

- non-employee as an author, and/or based on Astellas-sponsored research and/or related to Astellas products, therapeutic areas and/or business as specified in the scope below. This SOP is in alignment with POL-168 Global Publication Policy.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: high (words=695, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in the development, review and approval of all publications and associated supplemental materials (e.g., publication enhancements) in any language generated by an Astellas employee or non-employee as an author and/or based on Astellas-sponsored research (e.g., non-clinical, clinical (interventional and non-interventional studies), health economics and outcomes research) to be submitted for publication to a peer reviewed scientific journal or congress.

- This SOP also applies to:

- Publications based on Collaborative Research (CR) (see POL-AST-8264 Medical Affairs Collaborative Research Global Policy).

- Publications related to Astellas Primary Focus / Therapeutic Area (PF/TA) topics or business of Astellas-related topics with Astellas employees or non-employees as an author.

- Externally developed independent articles (e.g., invited reviews) where Astellas company review is being requested.

- Functional Units in scope for this SOP include, but are not limited to:

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Early Development

- Patient Centricity

- Market Access

- Rx+

- Data Science (DS)

- Clinical Operations

- Development Project Management (DPM)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Legal, including Intellectual Property Development & Commercial (IP DC)

- Divisions under the Chief Scientific Officer (CScO) including Development Project Management (DPM)

- Divisions under the Chief Manufacturing Officer (CMfgO) including Development Project Management (DPM)

- For Alliance products, where Astellas has a co-research, co-development, co-commercialization, co-promotion, or collaboration agreement, Astellas endeavors to agree with the other company(ies) or party(ies) on the general preconditions pertaining to the publication process (i.e., alignment on a publication plan, and right to review publications led by the Alliance partner) to be governed by a publication clause in the Alliance Agreement or a mutually agreeable Inter-Company Publication Charter. Individual publications will be under publication process governance from the company who leads the publication. For all Astellas-led publications, all steps defined in this SOP on requirements pertaining to the development and approval of individual publications must be implemented in full.

- Astellas operates in many different countries and this SOP establishes a global minimum standard for conducting publication activities worldwide. Where an Astellas company operates in a country with an applicable local law, rule, regulation, Code or Guideline that sets a higher standard than this SOP, the Astellas company must comply with the higher local standard.

- This SOP is not applicable to publications derived from

- Material Transfer Agreement (MTA)-based research

- SOP-752 Investigator Initiated Trials for Compounds in Development

- SOP-714 Medical Affairs Grants for Research (Investigator Sponsored Research (ISR)

- SOP-1943 Medical Affairs Sponsorships for Research

- SOP-3050 Medical Affairs Led HCP to HCP Educational Activity

- SOP-1945 Medical Affairs Grants for Education

- Corporate Communications (e.g., press releases, investor communications)

- POL-392 Global Policy for Creation, Review, and Approval of Materials

- white papers

- open and closed symposia

- SOP-3061 Review and Approval of Medical Affairs Materials

- publications designated as promotional materials (e.g., publications based on market research results, commercial sponsored consensus statements or Astellas-sponsored journal supplements). Those publications must be reviewed and approved according to applicable local policies and procedures on promotional review.

- research results disclosure on public websites for registered trials as per POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information.

- As defined in POL-AST-8437 Global Policy on Enhancing Astellas Stakeholder Engagement (EASE) and POL-168, colleagues whose job / roles are primarily to support sales, marketing, or other strategic commercial activities may not influence content development, review, or approval for biomedical publications. Therefore, Marketing/Brand Leads may not serve as reviewers or approvers of publications. However, Marketing/Brand Leads may provide strategic insights on information needs and target audience for publication planning purposes, as well as planned use of publications.

- When HEOR resources are unavailable, local Market Access teams can be involved in data generation and associated scientific publication planning activities for non-product related epidemiology, disease-state, or economic evidence.  Market Access may also serve as authors on a publication where International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) criteria are met.

- Any publications based on Market Access-led evidence generation and targeted to peer-reviewed journals or international/regional congresses must adhere to this SOP and be led by the Scientific Publication team. For any market access led publication targeted to a local (single country) congress, Market Access is accountable to ensure adherence to necessary standards when Scientific Publication team support is not available.

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List. Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document.

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Astellas sponsored study/research | A research project (including clinical trials) where Astellas is the Sponsor and takes responsibility for the initiation, management, and/or financing. |
| Candidate-Nomination (CN) | The decision point when an asset has demonstrated sufficient confidence in the therapeutic hypothesis, modality, and potential value to justify investment towards Investigational New Drug (IND) applications; particularly investment in drug substance to support IND enabling studies. (See POL-996 CN Declaration Committee Policy) |
| Clinical Publication | A publication that is based on data generated from Astellas-sponsored research in humans or using human materials and/or data, including but not limited to translational science studies, Phase 1-4 clinical trials, non-interventional studies (e.g., non-interventional post-authorization safety studies), pharmacokinetic analyses, post hoc and meta-analyses, database analyses of health outcomes, other types of Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR), or registry data. |
| Encore Publication | A repeated presentation of data at different congresses to reach different audiences (provided allowable by the congress and that copyright requirements are respected). An encore presentation contains the same data as the original publication. An encore translation must utilize a certified translation of the original publication from a qualified/accredited translation agency/translator. |
| Non-Astellas Led Publication | Publication on Astellas products or TA of interest that have not been developed by Astellas such as publications developed by: / Alliance Partner, / Investigator-led publication from collaborative research, / Investigator who develops a publication based on Astellas-sponsored research, and / Independent publications (e.g., request for data accuracy check of an independent review article or invited external presentation on or related to an Astellas product). |
| Non-Clinical Publication | A publication that is based on data generated from Astellas-sponsored non-clinical research. |
| Publication | Manuscripts (e.g., primary, secondary, review article, letter to the editor), abstracts and presentations, that are made publicly accessible either through open access, journal subscription or meeting registration, and are generally subject to external review prior to being made publicly available. This typically includes peer-review for manuscripts and a review process for abstracts, which result in an invitation for presentation at a scientific or medical conference. Authors are selected according to the ICMJE criteria and any congress- or journal-specific guidance. / NOTE: Appropriate scientific rigor, quality, and ethical standards should be applied to all research targeted for publication to scientific journals/congresses. |
| Simple Publication | A publication that meets all of the following requirements: / Always authored by an Astellas employee or non-employee, and / Not based on Astellas-sponsored non-clinical or clinical research, including post hoc and meta-analyses. / Publication examples: / Astellas-related business topics. / Publications initiated prior to author joining Astellas. / General statistical methodology. / General pharmacology model, general pharmacometric modeling and simulation methodology. / Overview of best practices at a professional conference. |
| Translation of Publication | A non-English translation of an existing publication to be submitted to a non-English language congress or journal to reach different audiences (provided it is allowable by the congress/ journal and copyright requirements are respected).  Must utilize a certified translation of the original language publication from a qualified/accredited translation agency/translator. |

## SECTION 5: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Astellas Author | Astellas employee or non-employee who is an author as defined in the SOP. |
| Author(s) | Person(s) named on the byline of a publication and controls decisions regarding the publication, including but not limited to content, target journal or congress and order of names on the byline. All authors are responsible for disclosing financial or other potential conflicts of interest that might be perceived to bias their work, as required by the pertinent congress or journal. / NOTE: Pursuant to the ICMJE criteria, general supervision of the research group that is conducting or supervising a project is not sufficient for authorship. Similarly, participation solely in the acquisition of funding or collection of data does not justify authorship. |
| Department Head | Department-specific function head who conducts publication approval. |
| Designee | Officially and knowingly agrees to fulfill the roles and/or actions on behalf of someone else (e.g., of the designator). The designator is ultimately responsible for the roles and actions fulfilled by the designee. |
| Intellectual Property (IP) | A person(s) who conducts an IP review/approval and has knowledge of the intellectual property under review. |
| Lead Author | Directs content development of the publication and takes a lead role on behalf of the full author group. |
| Lead Statistician* | Ensures statistical methodology and data interpretation are consistent with the Astellas clinical study report or other Astellas reviewed analyses and summaries. Provides source data, figures, and analyses as needed. |
| Medical Writer | Provides publication writing support if agreed to by authors and under their guidance. |
| Presenter | A person who presents the content of the publication at a congress on behalf of the authors. |
| Publication Lead | An individual who is responsible for overseeing the development of a publication. (For English language publications, Scientific Publications personnel are publication leads. For non-English language publications, local affiliate or regional tactic owners are the publication leads.) |
| Reviewer | Assesses publication in the capacity of a Subject Matter Expert (SME). |
| Study/Activity Lead* | Medical Lead, medical monitor, or designee from protocol design and/or study team, or the HEOR lead from the protocol design team, or other Astellas personnel, leading an activity that results in data generation. |

- Attachment 1 â€“ List of Publication and Publication Proposal Approvers and Reviewers

- *Astellas reviewers are to review and QC draft publications per their respective area of expertise.

- ** N/A for Non-Astellas Led publications

- Attachment 2 â€“ Publication Proposal Form

- Attachment 3 â€“ Study/Activity Lead Author Selection and Identification

- Study/Activity Lead:  In the table below, please provide a list of potential author names and mark their contributions for the above study/activity.

- *Per the first ICMJE criteria, authors are selected based on substantial contributions to:

- Conception or design of the work

- Example:  Contributing intellectual input into the protocol. However, contributing to the protocol development process alone, such as medical writing, does not constitute â€œconception or design of the work.â€

- Acquisition of data

- Example:  Scientifically relevant decisions regarding study conduct. However, execution of study procedures, in and of itself, does not constitute â€œacquisition of data.â€ Number of subjects enrolled into a study alone does not qualify one for authorship.

- Analysis of data

- Example:  Conception of analyses (creation of SAP and data table and figure shells) and ensuring that the scientific methodology is sufficient to allow for sound and accurate interpretation of the results. However, execution of SAP deliverables (such as programmers) in and of itself does not constitute â€œanalysis of data.â€

- Interpretation of data

- Example:  Provide scholarly relevant perspective and context to results.

- Attachment 4 â€“ Authorship Invitation/Agreement

- On behalf of <insert name of Astellas group>, I would like to invite you to be an author on a <publication type; insert as many types as covered under this agreement> based on data from <drug name> <study ISN#/Acronym Study> entitled, <working title>.

- If you are interested and available to commit to active participation in development of this publication, as well as any required resubmissions or presentations, permitted congress encores, or permitted publication translations, please respond to this email and indicate whether you accept this invitation by replying â€œI Acceptâ€.

- For publications based on Astellas sponsored research, Astellas follows the authorship criteria established by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE), unless the target congress or journal have different requirements:

- substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND

- drafting the work or reviewing it critically for important intellectual content; AND

- final approval of the version to be published; AND

- Accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring the questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved.

- All authors must fulfil all authorship criteria; failure to fulfil any of the four criteria will result in removal of the author from the publication.  The authors are solely responsible for the opinions, judgments and data expressed, presented, or implied in this publication (and related resubmissions encores or translations).

- In due course, you will receive confidential information and/or data supporting the development of this publication. This information and/or data is the property of Astellas which you can use solely for the development of this(ese) publication(s).

- As an author, you will be required to disclose to the target congress or journal any potential conflicts of interest, including pertinent financial or personal relationships that may be perceived to be a source of bias, using the ICMJE Disclosure of Interest form, and/or any other forms required by the applicable congress or journal.

- No compensation shall be made to you for any author or publication related activities except for the reimbursement for reasonable travel and related out-of-pocket expenses that are incurred by the presenting author in performance of the presentation at a congress (the â€œTravel Expensesâ€), as per Astellas policy. Such reimbursement is contingent upon pre-approval by Astellas and receipt of adequate supporting documentation (including, without limitation, copies of receipts).

- Attachment 4 â€“ Authorship Invitation/Agreement continued

- Any remuneration (payments to the author) will be reported publicly, as required by law. Astellas considers funded medical writing support for publication development (for US HCPs) and financial

- support for Travel Expenses by the presenting author to be a Transfer of Value to the author, and thus reportable according to the local rules and regulations.

- During the course of this agreement, Astellas will collect and process personal information for the purposes of managing the logistics of your participation in the publication process including reimbursement of approved out-of-pocket travel expenses, documentation of required review & approval processes and general management of any publications or presentations in which you will participate. By agreeing to participate, you also provide your agreement to the above processing of your personal information by Astellas, its affiliates and its agencies and service providers, including your agreement to any transfers of your personal information to countries beyond your country of residence. | Number of Authors | No policies should arbitrarily limit author numbers (3) / However, it is judicious to assign study and publication responsibilities so that the number of contributors in a functional area is reasonable. It is not permissible to divide professional responsibilities intentionally to disqualify or reduce the number of sponsor authors. |
| Author Sequence | The significance of author sequence may vary by scientific specialty and therapeutic area. Those who made the most contributions should be credited accordingly. The authors should agree to byline sequence, and the lead author may settle disputes. However, deferring to a neutral criterion such as alphabetical or reverse alphabetical order is recommended in cases of equal contributions |
| Addition of Authors After Submission | If the work to be published substantially changes in response to peer review (e.g., adding or removing analyses), the addition of an author might be considered as consistent with journal guidelines. All authors must agree to such a change. Author lists should remain consistent for a specific dataset, and encore presentations should list the same authors as the original presentation. Direct translations of presentations by nonauthor presenters for local language conferences may be needed, as permitted by the conference. |
| Death or Incapacity of an Author | Should a qualified author die or become incapacitated during publication development, they may be retained on the author byline if the journal or conference permits, with the agreement of the remaining authors. Consultation should be made to determine whether copyright transfer is necessary and, if so, who will execute it |
| Change of Affiliation | Change of affiliation is not a disqualification for authorship but may impede the ability of an otherwise qualified author to fulfill responsibilities. Reasonable efforts should be made to include all people who made intellectual contributions to study design, analysis, and/or data interpretation as authors. Listed affiliations should reflect author positions during the work to be published and be specified in the author agreement (if applicable). Footnotes may be used to designate current affiliations. ORCID numbers are recommended. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=71, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Policy (POL) is to establish the principles for preparation and approval of dossiers for Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Agencies, Value Evidence Assessment Committees (VEACs) or country-specific equivalent authorities such as pricing and reimbursement authorities.

- This POL is aligned with POL-AST-8437 Global Policy on Enhancing Astellas Stakeholder Engagement (EASE), SOP-1541 Development and Maintenance of the Core Value Dossier Procedure and SOP-967 Post Hoc Analysis initiated by Medical Affairs.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=104, tables=0)_

- This POL applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in preparation, review and approval of product dossiers for submission to HTA Agencies/VEACs or country-specific equivalent authorities to request technological scientific/economic appraisal of the evidence, to seek pricing and/or reimbursement recommendations and/or positive formulary listing from National or Regional authority(ies) or Payer organization(s).

- For products where Astellas has a co-marketing/co-promotion, co-development or co-research agreement with another company (â€œAlliance Companyâ€), Astellas must endeavour to agree with the Alliance Company on a common policy or guideline that adheres to these principles as a minimum standard and as stipulated in the terms of the agreement.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: low (words=8, tables=0)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

---

## SECTION 5: PRINCIPLES

_Slug: principles_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: low (words=0, tables=0)_

---

## SECTION 6: Overview

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=159, tables=0)_

- Dossiers are submitted by the responsible Astellas affiliate to HTA Agencies/VEACs or country-specific equivalent authorities to seek either appraisal of the evidence base for the product or technology (e.g., Institute for Clinical and Economic Review (ICER) in the USA, National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), Scottish Medicines Consortium (SMC), Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss (GBA), tandvÃ¥rds- och lÃ¤kemedelsfÃ¶rmÃ¥nsverket (TLV), Haute AutoritÃ© de SantÃ© (HAS), Canadian Agency for Drugs and Technologies in Health (CADTH)), to seek pricing and/or reimbursement recommendations, and/or to gain a formulary listing from National or Regional authority(ies) or Payer organization(s) (e.g., United Health Group, Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee (PBAC), Health Insurance Review & Assessment Agency (HIRA), Health Technology Assessment Institute, Instituto de EvaluaciÃ³n TecnolÃ³gica en Salud (IETS), National Committee for Health Technology Incorporation (CONITEC)).

- HTA Agency/VEAC and/or other pricing/reimbursement submission dossiers may include clinical, medical, humanistic, health economic, epidemiological, societal, and pricing information, and are generally submitted in concert with the regulatory submission timelines for a product.

---

## SECTION 7: Preparation and Approval of the Submission Dossier

_Slug: preparation_and_approval_of_the_submission_dossier_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=258, tables=0)_

- The submission dossier is developed by the Astellas affiliate lead according to local requirements, using information from the Core Value Dossier (CVD) and aligned with the integrated Global Brand Plan (iGBP) and the integrated Global Value Plan (iGVP), if existing, and associated strategic documents.

- When preparing an HTA Agency/VEAC submission documents, the following core principles must be followed:

- Medical, health economic and other evidence must be aligned and consistent with the most recent Global Product Strategy Team (GPST) strategy, iGBP, iGVP, if existing, and CVD.

- Submissions must be completed according to local country requirements, using the templates, formats and timeframes specified by the relevant HTA Agency/VEAC or country-specific equivalent authorities. Gaining pre-submission advice is recommended, where possible, and will follow local HTA-specific guidance for the conduct, where required.

- The submission dossier must be reviewed and approved by the regional and affiliate Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Lead, regional Medical Affairs (MA) Therapeutic Area (TA) Lead, and Market Access (MAx) Archetype Access Lead (AAL) or MAx Regional Implementation Lead.

- Prior to external dissemination, the dossier must undergo any applicable local or regional approval process and the appropriate quality and compliance checks.

- Any deviations from the pre-defined GPST strategy will need assessment and prior approval from both the GPST and the Global Value Team (GVT). The affiliate lead is responsible for informing the GVT and GPST of the reasons behind the proposed strategy.

- For in scope products/technologies that do not have a GPST and/or GVT, a committee of similar composition will be established for the purpose of these activities.

---

## SECTION 8: Preparation and Approval of Local Adaptations

_Slug: preparation_and_approval_of_local_adaptations_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-265.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: high (words=403, tables=0)_

- Tailoring of data/information to produce supplemental content for the submission dossier in order to meet local country requirements of an HTA Agency/VEAC or country-specific equivalent authorities must be consistent with the global GPST strategy, iGBP and aligned to the CVD.

- Local team(s) must inform the GVT of preparation of such supplemental content prior to submission. As per best practices, decisions should be documented and uploaded to the designated repository.

- Local adaptations, that are aligned with the GPST strategy, iGBP and the CVD (and the core health economic (HE) model) are reviewed and approved by appropriate MA and Commercial personnel at region and/or affiliate level.

- Examples of such local adaptations may include, but are not limited to:

- Addition of local epidemiology data

- Reference to local treatment pathways/algorithms and treatment guidelines

- Information on local healthcare costs

- Adaptation of the core economic model based on local data and local requirements aligned with key assumptions in the economic model or structure of the model

- Local budget impact model calculations/information

- Post-hoc analysis (e.g., country-specific subgroup analyses) that are included in the CVD

- Minor editorial changes to the value proposition that reflect the HTA Agency/VEAC needs or requests

- Translations

- However, if local adaptations do not align with the GPST strategy, iGBP and CVD (and the core economic model), the local adaptation must be reviewed and approved by the GVT co-chairs prior to submission.

- Examples of such local adaptations may include, but are not limited to:

- Scientific and medical data that are not included in the CVD (e.g., new/additional post-hoc analysis (refer to SOP-967), other new/additional data from internal or external sources) that significantly changes the value message

- Significant changes to the value proposition and supporting evidence defined in the CVD and deviations from the iGBP

- Variations from the overall product strategy and positioning, as defined by the GPST and iGBP

- Change in key assumptions in the core economic model or structure of the model

- GVT co-chairs may reject a local adaptation request if it is deemed that the content may negatively impact the global GPST strategy. Approval or rejection of a local adaptation by GVT co-chairs must be documented in the GVT meeting minutes and the affiliate lead and the GPST must be informed. As per best practices, rational for the rejection must also be documented and uploaded to the designated repository.

- Final submission material must be retained in the designated repository considering the confidential nature of some materials.

---

Q&A CTR: The documentation required to show compliance of the IMP and AxMP with GMP is outlined in Chapter IX and Annex 1 section F of the Clinical Trials Regulation: / â€¢ For IMPs authorised in the EU (even if not manufactured in the EU) no documentation is required. / â€¢ For IMPSs that are not authorised in the EU and do not have a marketing authorisation from a third country that is party to ICH, and are not manufactured in the EU, an authorisation referred to in article 61(1) and a QP declaration of GMP equivalence is required. In the latter case, if a Mutual recognition Agreement (MRA) covering also clinical trials is in place with the particular country, the latter declaration is not required if the MRA provides for GMP equivalence already. / â€¢ In all other cases, an authorisation according to article 61 of the Clinical trial Regulation) is required. Information regarding the GMP compliance of the active pharmaceutical ingredients is not required by the CTR (and can therefore not be required by the Member States Concerned.) |

_Signals: medium (words=99, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Policy (POL) is to make clinical trial information and results more widely available to researchers, healthcare professionals, patients, and interested members of the public to benefit public health. Therefore, Astellas is committed to publicly sharing data on clinical trials that are sponsored by Astellas. To meet this commitment, Astellas complies with relevant laws, regulatory requirements, and industry guidance for registration of clinical trial information and disclosure of clinical trial results, as well as the POL-534 Astellas Group Code of Conduct.

- Further details can be found in SOP-1161 Process for Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: POL-100.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=165, tables=0)_

- This policy applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in the clinical trial disclosure process.

- This policy applies to all Astellas products, including those in-licensed from non-Astellas companies. All clinical trials and non-interventional studies sponsored by Astellas are assessed for disclosure requirements. Interventional clinical trials are registered with results disclosed as stated within this policy and as required by local/regional laws or regulations.

- For products where Astellas has a co-research, co-development or co-marketing/co-promotion agreement, it is recognized that the responsibility for disclosure is dependent on the agreement between parties. Astellas will endeavor to gain agreement on the principles set forth in this policy in arrangements with third parties, but at all times Astellas complies with the relevant laws and regulatory guidance.

- This policy does not apply to investigator-initiated studies for products in development or investigator sponsored research for marketed products, as such, studies are not sponsored or conducted by Astellas. Astellas, however, encourages investigators to register these clinical studies and disclose the results.

## SECTION 6: Registration of Clinical Trials

_Slug: registration_of_clinical_trials_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-100.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=114, tables=0)_

- Astellas commits to registering all interventional clinical trials with a medicinal product sponsored by Astellas that seek to evaluate the safety and/or efficacy profile of an Astellas owned or in-licensed product. Clinical trials sponsored by Astellas that are covered under this policy are registered on a publicly accessible clinical trial registry (e.g., www.clinicaltrials.gov). In addition, other Astellas sponsored studies (e.g., non-interventional studies, medical device, early access) are included in national/regional registries, if required by local/regional laws or regulations.

- Astellas recognizes that there are registries that extract information from various sources. Astellas cannot guarantee these registries are maintained with updated information or their accuracy, and accordingly disclaims any liability arising from use of these registries.

---

## SECTION 7: Posting of Clinical Trial Results

_Slug: posting_of_clinical_trial_results_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-100.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=282, tables=0)_

- Astellas commits to disclosing summary results for all phase 1 to 4 interventional clinical trials with a medicinal product sponsored by Astellas, conducted in the target patient population, with Astellas products that have health authority (HA) approval. In addition, summary results for other Astellas sponsored studies (e.g., non-interventional studies, medical device, early access) are disclosed on national/regional registries, if required by local/regional laws or regulations.

- Summary results and a plain language summary are posted on clinical trial results website(s) (www.clinicaltrials.astellas.com and/or www.trialsummaries.com/Home/LandingPage) for clinical trials conducted with medicinal products that receive initial HA approval after January 1, 2014. Summary results are publicly disclosed within 3 months after initial HA approval is granted for studies with an end of study (EOS) clinical study report (CSR) available at the time of the first HA approval, within 30 days of CSR EOS for studies without a EOS CSR at time of HA approval, or within 12 months after trial completion for clinical trials with a medicinal product conducted with product formulations and indications that previously received HA approval. Additionally, summary results are posted on a publicly accessible clinical trial results website for trials with a medicinal product conducted with products that received initial HA approval from November 1, 2008 through December 31, 2013.

- Summary results and a plain language summary are also disclosed on clinical trial results website(s) for clinical trials conducted with medicinal products that are terminated during development after January 1, 2014. Results are disclosed for completed trials within 12 months after medicinal product development is terminated. Results are disclosed within 12 months after trial completion for clinical trials that are ongoing at the time that development of the medicinal product is terminated.

## SECTION 9: Scientific Community Access to Clinical Trial Data

_Slug: scientific_community_access_to_clinical_trial_data_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: POL-100.docx | docx | Section 9_

_Signals: medium (words=151, tables=0)_

- Subject to compliance with the applicable laws and regulations relevant to protection of personal data, Astellas provides a platform (www.clinicalstudydatarequest.com) where researchers may request access to participant level data, trial level data and protocols from Astellas sponsored clinical trials with a medicinal product conducted in patients that are completed after January 1, 2010.

- Access to this data is granted for medicinal products and indications approved in any country after the request has been reviewed and approved by an independent panel of experts (â€œScientific Review Boardâ€) based on scientific merit and the qualifications of the researcher. Access is given by Astellas after review and approval by the Scientific Review Board and execution of a data sharing agreement.

- Before participant-level data is shared, it is anonymized to respect the rights of the clinical trial subjects to privacy and to protection of their personal health information in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=50, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define the process by which Astellas complies with the relevant laws, regulatory requirements and industry guidance driving clinical study registration and public disclosure of clinical study results as described in POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=83, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in the clinical study disclosure process.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Clinical Operations

- Data Science

- Early Development

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Research

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Alliance Management

- Intellectual Property

- Corporate Advocacy & Relations

- This SOP does not apply to investigator-initiated studies for products in development or investigator sponsored research for marketed products, as such studies are not sponsored or conducted by Astellas.

## SECTION 7: Assess Registration Requirements

_Slug: assess_registration_requirements_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=206, tables=1)_

- All Astellas sponsored interventional clinical trials with a medicinal product are registered. In addition, other Astellas sponsored studies (e.g., non-interventional, medical device or early access studies) are registered in compliance with local/regional laws or regulations. CT Lead will interact with the therapeutic area Publications Lead and Study Team Key Contact when there is a request to register an Astellas sponsored study that does not require registration per POL-100 or local/regional laws and regulations.

- Each Astellas sponsored study is assessed by the CT Lead to determine if there are registration requirements. The assessment indicates participating countries, which databases and/or countries have relevant registration requirements, and when the registration activities must be completed. STL-2981 Clinical Study Disclosure Registration Country Requirements must be signed no later than 30 days prior to planned First Subject First Visit (FSFV) or the start of data collection (if final protocol is available) or within 7 days of protocol finalization (if within 30 days of planned FSFV or the start of data collection). If all participating countries are unknown prior to planned FSFV, STL-2981 should be signed off prior to planned FSFV with current, known participating countries. A revised STL-2981 should be completed when additional countries have been selected and confirmed for study participation.

**Table 1 (assess_registration_requirements_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Notify the Clinical Transparency department of an approved protocol synopsis within 30 days of approval by either of the following: / Confirmation of delivery of the approved protocol synopsis via automated notification from an Electronic Document Management System (EDMS), or / Email to ClinicalTrialRegistration@astellas.com, including the approved protocol synopsis and an expected translation completion date, if applicable. / NOTE:  For studies that do not have a protocol synopsis approval process, provide a draft of the full protocol. |
| CT Lead | Assess registration requirements for the clinical study, including country-specific registration requirements using STL-2981. |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Notify the Clinical Transparency department of an approved protocol within 7 days of approval, by either of the following: / Confirmation of delivery of the approved protocol via automated notification from an EDMS, or / Email to ClinicalTrialRegistration@astellas.com, including the approved protocol and an expected translation completion date, if applicable. |
| CT Lead | Review the final protocol to confirm: / If a non-interventional study is classified as a Post Authorization Safety Study (PASS) or Post Authorization Efficacy / Effectiveness Study (PAES) potentially requiring registration on the HMA-EMA Catalogue of real-world data (RWD) studies. / If the study has the finalized list of participating countries. |
| CT Lead | Notify the Study Team Key Contact of any known registration requirements using unsigned STL-2981 and request that Study Team Key Contact or designee signs and sends the document back. |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Review and sign STL-2981 to acknowledge registration requirements and provide to the CT Lead. / STL-2981 must be signed no later than 30 days prior to planned First Subject First Visit (FSFV) or the start of data collection (if final protocol is available) or within 7 days of protocol finalization (if within 30 days of planned FSFV or the start of data collection). / If all participating countries are unknown prior to planned FSFV, STL-2981 should be signed off prior to planned FSFV with current, known participating countries. |
| CT Lead | Sign STL-2981 and file documentation associated with the registration assessment in the Trial Master File (TMF). |
| CT Lead | Complete a revised STL-2981 following steps 5-7, as applicable, e.g., Study Team Key Contact changes before all requirements have been completed, and/or additional countries have been selected and confirmed for study participation. |

## SECTION 8: Notification and Review of EudraCT or EU CTIS Application/Study Milestones

_Slug: notification_and_review_of_eudract_or_eu_ctis_application_study_milestones_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=182, tables=1)_

- The EudraCT (for trials conducted under the EU Directive) and the EU CTIS (for trials conducted under the EU Clinical Trial Regulation) are the European databases for all interventional clinical trials on medicinal products authorized in the EU and outside the EU/European Economic Area (EEA) if they are part of a Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP).

- For registrations in the EudraCT database or EU CTIS, refer to WI-AST-14598 Develop, Submit, and Maintain Clinical Trial Authorizations and WI-AST-14676 Update the Clinical Trials Information System. Also, refer to STL-5000 EudraCT Number Application and Database Instructions for EudraCT registrations only.

- Pediatric clinical studies conducted anywhere in the world (fulfilling article 45 and 46 of the Paediatric Regulation), with products that are approved by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) that may or may not be part of a PIP as agreed with the EMA, are required to be registered in the EudraCT or EU CTIS.

- Study notifications (i.e., study event/milestone dates) are required to be reported to member states and made public via the EU CTIS. Refer to SOP-1687 Submission of Clinical Study Documentation to Ethics Committees.

**Table 1 (notification_and_review_of_eudract_or_eu_ctis_application_study_milestones_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| RRL or RSTM | Notify the Clinical Transparency Department (ClinicalTrialRegistration@astellas.com) of clinical studies that are being registered on EudraCT or EU CTIS by doing the following: / Provide the CT Lead with a copy or link to the core part of the EudraCT or EU CTIS Clinical Trial Application (CTA) form. / Confirm if the clinical trial is included in an approved PIP. |
| CT Lead | Review the core part of the EudraCT or EU CTIS application for consistency with the CT.gov registration, when possible. |
| CT Lead | Provide comments, if applicable, to RRL or RSTM on core part of the EudraCT or EU CTIS application form. |
| RRL or RSTM, Study Team Key Contact or designee | During the conduct of the study, notify the Clinical Transparency Department (ClinicalTrialRegistration@astellas.com) of an updated EudraCT/ EU CTIS CTA form or study event/milestone dates of clinical studies that will be or have been submitted and will be made public on EU CTIS. |
| CT Lead | Review updated EudraCT/ EU CTIS CTA form or study event/milestone dates for consistency with the CT.gov registration, when possible. |
| CT Lead | Provide comments, if applicable, to RRL or RSTM, Study Team Key Contact or designee. |

## SECTION 9: Notification of Changes

_Slug: notification_of_changes_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 9_

_Signals: high (words=368, tables=1)_

- All changes during the study should be communicated to the Clinical Transparency department for assessment of changes to the study information on public databases/registries, as applicable.

- Any revision to the following fields/sections (or equivalent) of a registration are considered significant with the exception of grammar or rephrasing information:

- Collaborators

- Primary and Secondary Outcome Measures: Title, Description and Timeframe

- Milestone (timeline) updates, including changing from anticipated to actual:

- Study Start Date (estimated date when the study will be open for recruitment, later updated to actual date when the first subject is enrolled)

- Primary Completion Date (date the final subject will be or was examined or received an intervention for final collection of data for all primary outcome measures)

- Study Completion Date (date the final subject will be or was examined or received an intervention for final collection of data for all primary and secondary outcome measures and adverse events)

- Why Study Suspended, Terminated or Withdrawn

- Arms: Title and Description

- Interventions: Name and Other Name

- CT.gov requires that the registration be updated within 15 or 30 days when specific changes occur (see below). The Study Team Key Contact should consider the timing requirement for updating the CT.gov registration when notifying the Clinical Transparency department of changes. For specific steps in updating CT.gov registrations, refer to Section V.F.

- The items listed below require an update to the CT.gov registration within 15 days:

- Response to CT.gov Quality Assurance (QA) Review Major Comments

- Known errors in registration (until all required information has been submitted and corrections have made or addressed in response to any CT.gov QA Review Major Comments)

- The items listed below require an update to the CT.gov registration within 30 days:

- Changes due to protocol amendments

- Responsible party contact

- Availability of expanded access

- Human Subject Review Board Status

- Study Start date

- Overall recruitment status (A study is noted as â€œrecruitingâ€ after the first site is initiated)

- Recruitment status for each site (Sites participating in the study are noted as â€œrecruitingâ€ after the site is initiated)

- Primary Completion date (Estimated dates are updated to actual dates when achieved)

- Study Completion date (Estimated dates are updated to actual dates when achieved)

- Actual enrollment (after enrollment ends)

- Intervention Name (after non-proprietary name is established)

**Table 1 (notification_of_changes_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CT Lead | Create a study-specific STL-2982 Study Notifications for Clinical Study Disclosure. |
| CT Lead | Distribute the study-specific STL-2982 to the Study Team Key Contact or designee. / For studies that do not require registration on any database, distribute Study Notifications for Clinical Study Disclosure after requirements are assessed (refer to Section V.A.) / For studies that do have registration requirements on any database, distribute Study Notifications for Clinical Study Disclosure after the first registration requirement is completed (refer to Section V.D., V.E., and V.F.) |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Notify Clinical Transparency using the study-specific STL-2982 when there are changes to the protocol/study. |

---

- Interventional clinical trials within a medicinal product are registered on the ClinicalTrials.gov publicly accessible internet database. | Team Reviewers | Review the CT.gov registration for accuracy and send comments to the CT Lead. |

| CT Lead | Release the registration for public posting on CT.gov no later than 21 days after enrollment begins (date of the first signed Informed Consent Form) or data collection begins (for non-interventional studies registered on CT.gov). |

## SECTION 11: Complete Country-Specific (or Other) Registrations and Updates

_Slug: complete_country_specific_or_other_registrations_and_updates_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 11_

_Signals: high (words=415, tables=1)_

- Studies are registered and updated on Country-Specific or other databases when required by law or regulation, including the HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies. For requirements related to the HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies, refer to policy POL-211.

- Country-specific databases or other databases are populated for registration and updates as listed below.

- Information is automatically pulled/taken from the regulatory or IRB/IEC application and posted in the public database.

- Study Team Key Contact or designee is responsible for completing regulatory and IRB/IEC application and follow documented processes outside the scope of SOP-1161. If information is automatically pulled/taken from regulatory or IRB/IEC application and posted in a public database, the CT Lead reviews content before submission and records that regulatory or IRB/IEC submission/approval has occurred (for initial registration, on STL-2981). Some examples where information is automatically pulled/taken from the regulatory or IRB/IEC application and posted in a public database include:

- Europe: CTA populates EudraCT/EU CTIS via the EU-Clinical Trial Registry (EU-CTR)/EU CTIS public website.

- Germany: regulatory submission populates BfArM CUP for compassionate use studies.

- France: regulatory submission populates French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM) Website (in French) for cohort temporary authorization for use (cATU).

- Switzerland: IRB/IEC submission populates website known as Swiss National Clinical Trial Portal (SNCTP).

- United Kingdom: IRB/IEC submission populates Health Research Authority (HRA) website.

- Information is submitted directly to country-specific database (e.g., country-specific database is not automatically populated by regulatory or IRB/IEC application).

- Clinical Transparency is responsible for information submitted directly to a country-specific database, however the Study Team or designee may draft and/or submit to database. Some examples of information submitted directly to country-specific database include:

- China: chinadrugtrials.org.cn Europe: HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies

- Germany: Observational Studies (AWB) database

- Japan: jRCT

- South Korea: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS)

- Follow the below process when information is submitted directly to a country-specific database. Team review and Senior Management Approval is required when information cannot be sourced from CT.gov registration for initial registration. For updates, Team review and Senior Management Approval are required when changes not sourced from CT.gov registration are considered significant (see section V.C.).

- STL-2981 (see section V.A) documents how the database is populated on a country level (refer to signed STL-2981 section 1, What activity needs to be completed to meet registration requirement?). STL-2982 (see section V.C) documents the information (on a study level) that is required to be updated and the timing for updates when information is submitted directly to a country-specific database (not via regulatory or IRB/IEC applications).

**Table 1 (complete_country_specific_or_other_registrations_and_updates_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CT Lead | Facilitate submission of information directly to country-specific databases, including the HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (when required) according to STL-2981. This can include drafting the registration and/or completing a review and approval process. |
| CT Lead | Confirm that QC review of the country-specific registration is performed by the CT QC Reviewer; with findings resolved for registrations drafted by Clinical Transparency. |
| CT Lead | Complete submission or work with the Study Team Key Contact or designee to submit the registration to country-specific databases. |
| CT Lead | Respond to registration-related clarifications that must be addressed before the country-specific registration is made public (if applicable). |
| CT Lead | Archive appropriate documentation related to initial registration. |
| CT Lead | Complete STL-2981 with information related to submission of information directly to a country-specific database. |
| CT Lead | Confirm with the Study Team Key Contact and document on STL-2981 that any regulatory or IRB/IEC submission/approval has occurred. This should occur as soon as all requirements are completed (even if prior to end of enrollment) and no later than 30 days after the end of enrollment. |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Sign STL-2981 to acknowledge information supporting registration requirements was provided to Clinical Transparency. Send the signed STL-2981 back to the CT Lead. |
| CT Lead | Sign and file completed STL-2981 in the TMF. |
| CT Lead | Upon receipt of study changes via STL-2982, facilitate submission of updated information directly to country-specific databases, including the HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (when required). This can include drafting the updates and/or completing a review and approval process. |
| CT Lead | Confirm that QC review of the country-specific registration update is performed by the CT QC Reviewer, with findings resolved for registration updates drafted by Clinical Transparency. |
| CT Lead | Complete submission or work with the Study Team Key Contact or designee to submit the registration update to country-specific databases. |
| CT Lead | Archive appropriate documentation related to registration updates. |

## SECTION 12: Update CT.gov Registrations

_Slug: update_ct_gov_registrations_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 12_

_Signals: medium (words=68, tables=1)_

- The Study Team Key Contact or designee should notify Clinical Transparency using STL-2982 per step V.C.3. Determine if revisions are considered significant or non-significant according to section V.C.

- Significant update: If there is at least one change in any data fields in section V.C., the update is considered significant.

- Non-Significant update: If there are no changes in any data fields in section V.C., the update is considered non-significant.

**Table 1 (update_ct_gov_registrations_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CT Lead or designee | Check with the Study Team Key Contact within 180 days if registration has not been updated to see if any study changes and/or changes to the registration are required. |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Anytime during the study, confirm if changes are required and communicate changes via STL-2982. |
| CT Lead | Summarize any necessary updates to the CT.gov registration. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Perform QC review of the changes to the CT.gov registration. If there are no changes, proceed to step V.F.11. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Work with the CT Lead to resolve any findings. |
| CT Lead | Distribute the updates to the Team Reviewers if required. (Reference Section IV: Roles & Responsibilities on the required team reviewers for significant and non-significant changes). |
| Team Reviewers | Review the CT.gov registration for accuracy and send comments to the CT Lead. |
| CT Lead | Receive and reconcile comments/edits in consultation with the Team Reviewers, follow-up on any comments/edits and repeat review and QC steps until all comments/edits are addressed. |
| CT Lead | Request Senior Management approval of updates to the CT.gov registration if required. |
| Senior Management Approver | Review updates made to the CT.gov registration and notify the CT Lead of action taken (approve or reject): / If the updated registration is approved, proceed to step V.F.11. / If the updated registration is rejected, the CT Lead incorporates revisions and returns to step V.F.3. |
| CT Lead | Release the registration for public posting on CT.gov. |
| CT Lead | Notify the Study Team Key Contact when the registration update is complete and when it will be publicly disclosed. |
| CT Lead | File documentation associated with the registration update in the TMF. |

## SECTION 14: Assess Requirements for Disclosure of Results

_Slug: assess_requirements_for_disclosure_of_results_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 14_

_Signals: medium (words=124, tables=1)_

- Each Astellas sponsored study is assessed by the CT Lead to determine if there are results disclosure requirements. The assessment documents which databases and/or countries have relevant results disclosure requirements, and when the disclosure activities must be completed. The assessment is performed after the interim analysis data cutoff date (if applicable), primary completion date (if applicable) and after study completion (LSLV for the final analysis unless otherwise defined in the protocol) or when data collection is complete for non-interventional studies.

- Although assessments are performed for each Astellas sponsored study to determine if there are results disclosure requirements, Astellas does not mandate the disclosure of results for non-interventional, medical device or early access studies if there are no local/regional laws or regulations requiring these activities.

**Table 1 (assess_requirements_for_disclosure_of_results_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Study Team Key Contact or designee | Notify the Clinical Transparency Department after the interim analysis cutoff date (if applicable), primary completion date (if applicable) and study completion or when the end of data collection has occurred using study-specific STL-2982 as described in Section V.C.3. |
| CT Lead | Assess requirements for disclosure of results, including timelines for disclosure following approval or withdrawal of a new MAA, NDA/BLA or variation or project termination decision made by the Executive Committee or Kachi Committee (KC). |
| CT Lead | Refer to the final protocol to confirm if a non-interventional study has been classified as a PASS or PAES potentially requiring disclosure of results on the HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies or other register. |
| CT Lead | Notify the Study Team Key Contact of any known requirements to disclose results, including the need for a redacted Clinical Study Report (CSR) synopsis, plain language summary or other documents needed for Clinical Transparency. |
| CT Lead | File documentation associated with the disclosure assessment in the TMF. |
| CT Lead | Track the type and timing of results disclosure for each clinical study if disclosure or a request for delay is required. |

## SECTION 15: Disclose Results on Clinical Trial Results Websites

_Slug: disclose_results_on_clinical_trial_results_websites_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 15_

_Signals: medium (words=296, tables=1)_

- Publicly accessible clinical trial results websites (www.clinicaltrials.astellas.com and/or www.trialsummaries.com/Home/LandingPage) are used for disclosing the results of Astellas sponsored phase 1 to 4 interventional clinical trials with a medicinal product, conducted in the target patient population, with Astellas products that have HA approval.

- Results are disclosed for clinical studies conducted with medicinal products that receive initial HA approval after January 1, 2014. Results are disclosed in the form of a plain language summary (when permitted by local/regional law or regulation) and/or a CSR synopsis that is redacted according to industry accepted redacting principles. The redacted CSR synopsis is publicly disclosed within 3 months after initial HA approval is granted (i.e., first HA approval for a product) for studies with an end of study (EOS) CSR available at the time of the first HA approval, within 30 days of CSR EOS for studies without a EOS CSR at time of HA approval or within 12 months after study completion for clinical studies with a medicinal product conducted with product formulations and indications that previously received HA approval. Timing for posting the plain language summary may occur after the redacted CSR synopsis is publicly disclosed.

- Summary results are also posted on publicly accessible clinical trial results website(s) for clinical studies with a medicinal product conducted with products that received initial HA approval from November 1, 2008 through December 31, 2013.

- The plain language summary and redacted CSR synopsis are publicly disclosed for clinical studies conducted with medicinal products that are terminated during development after January 1, 2014. Results are disclosed for completed studies within 12 months after development of medicinal product is terminated. Results are disclosed within 12 months after study completion for clinical studies that are ongoing at the time that development of the medicinal product is terminated.

**Table 1 (disclose_results_on_clinical_trial_results_websites_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| MW Disclosure Document Lead | Notify the Clinical Transparency Department when the redacted CSR synopsis (or reissued CSR synopsis) and plain language summary are available. |
| CT Lead | Confirm that any data required to complete the disclosure of results is entered. |
| CT Lead | Confirm the redacted CSR synopsis (or reissued CSR synopsis) and plain language summary are uploaded to the website(s). |
| CT QC Reviewer | Perform QC review of the data entered and uploaded against the relevant, predetermined source of information for each data field. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Work with the CT Lead to resolve any findings. |
| CT Lead | Request Senior Management and collaborator approval (if applicable) to post the redacted CSR synopsis (or reissued CSR synopsis) and plain language summary on clinical trial results website(s). |
| Senior Management Approver | Review the request for disclosure of draft results on the website(s) and notify the CT Lead when approval is granted. |
| CT Lead | Confirm the results are released for public disclosure on the website(s). |
| CT Lead | Notify the department sponsoring the study when results are released on the website(s). |
| CT Lead | Instruct the Study Team Key Contact to notify the Clinical Transparency Department if the CSR is later reissued, requiring review and possibly an updated, redacted CSR synopsis and/or plain language summary. |
| CT Lead | Repeat the process for disclosing results on clinical trial results website(s), beginning with step V.I.1., if revisions were made to the CSR that affect the results that were posted. |
| CT Lead | File documentation associated with the disclosure in the TMF. |

---

## SECTION 16: Post a Delayed Disclosure on CT.gov (for applicable clinical trials)

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 16_

- An extension to the deadline for posting the results of applicable clinical trials on CT.gov may be granted when a written request is submitted that demonstrates good cause for the extension and provides an estimate of the date on which the results will be disclosed. Pending publication plans are not considered good cause for an extension. An extension may also be granted when an applicable clinical trial reaches its completion date before the product used in the trial is approved for use by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or when the trial evaluates a new use of an FDA-approved product.

**Table 1 (post_a_delayed_disclosure_on_ct_gov_for_applicable_clinical_trials_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CT Lead | Compile the data required to post a delayed disclosure on CT.gov. |
| CT Lead or designee | Complete data entry to post a delayed disclosure. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Perform QC review of the data entered against the data required to post a delayed disclosure. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Work with the CT Lead to resolve any findings. / If the delayed disclosure is a â€œcertificate of delayâ€ before the product is approved for use or when the clinical trial evaluates the new use of an FDA-approved product, proceed to step V.J.9. / For all other delayed disclosures, proceed to step V.J.5. |
| CT Lead | Distribute the data required to post a delayed disclosure to the Team Reviewers if a â€œgood cause extensionâ€ is being requested by the study team. |
| CT Lead | Request Senior Management approval and the collaborator approval (if applicable) to post the delayed disclosure if a â€œgood cause extensionâ€ is being requested. |
| Senior Management Approver | Review the request for delayed disclosure on CT.gov and notify the CT Lead of any revisions. |
| Senior Management Approver | Notify the CT Lead when the request to post a delayed disclosure is approved. |
| CT Lead | Release the delayed disclosure on CT.gov. |
| CT Lead | Notify the Study Team Key Contact when the delay has been accepted. |
| CT Lead | File documentation associated with the delayed disclosure in the TMF. |

## SECTION 17: Disclose Results on CT.gov or EudraCT/EU CTIS

_Slug: disclose_results_on_ct_gov_or_eudract_eu_ctis_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-1161 (5).docx | docx | Section 17_

_Signals: high (words=302, tables=1)_

- For clinical studies that meet the definition of â€œapplicable clinical trialâ€ under the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act (FDAAA) 2007 legislation and 42 CFR Part 11 (Final Rule effective 18 January 2017), summary results {consisting of a pre-defined data set, full final redacted protocol and redacted Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP)} must be posted on CT.gov. Timing for submission of results is at the earliest of the following:

- No later than 12 months after the primary completion date and until results have been submitted for all primary and secondary outcome measures and adverse events, for clinical trials conducted with product formulations and indications that previously received United States (US) NDA or BLA approval or termination of development of medicinal product.

- No later than 30 days after US NDA/BLA approval, for applicable clinical trials conducted with the newly approved product.

- No later than 2 years after a request for delayed disclosure is submitted.

- Results are also submitted for applicable clinical trials after FDA issues a letter ending the NDA/BLA review cycle without approval or when the application seeking approval is withdrawn.

- For clinical studies that are within scope according to the EU clinical trial legislation, summary results (consisting of a pre-defined data set and/or summary results document and when required, a plain language summary) are submitted via the EudraCT or EU CTIS database. Results must be submitted within 6 months (for pediatric clinical studies) or within 1 year (for adult clinical studies) after trial completion in the EU or as defined by the protocol. In addition, interim results must be submitted within 1 year of interim analysis date as defined by the protocol. The EU clinical trial legislation is applicable regardless of the productâ€™s HA approval status. Discontinued products are also within scope for disclosure of results under the EU clinical trial legislation.

**Table 1 (disclose_results_on_ct_gov_or_eudract_eu_ctis_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CT Lead | Draft the CT.gov/EudraCT/EU CTIS Data Disclosure Worksheet indicating where source data needed for the disclosure is located. / NOTE: Refer to the disclosure of results on other databases (e.g., EudraCT/EU CTIS or CT.gov, if applicable) for consistency. |
| CT Lead | Complete data entry and/or document upload for the disclosure of results. |
| CT QC Reviewer | Perform QC review of the data entered and/or document upload against the CT.gov/EudraCT/EU CTIS Data Disclosure Worksheet and supporting documentation (e.g., Clinical Study Report, SAP, etc.). |
| CT QC Reviewer | Work with the CT Lead to resolve any findings. |
| CT Lead | For pre-defined data set results: Distribute the draft results and supporting documentation to the Team Reviewers. |
| Team Reviewers | For pre-defined data set results: Review the draft results and send comments to the CT Lead. |
| CT Lead | For pre-defined data set results: Receive and reconcile comments/edits in consultation with the Team Reviewers, follow-up on any comments/edits and repeat review until all comments/edits are addressed. |
| CT Lead | Request Senior Management approval of the draft results. |
| Senior Management Approver | Review the draft results and notify the CT Lead of any revisions. |
| Senior Management Approver | Notify the CT Lead when the disclosure of results is approved. |
| CT Lead | Release the results for public disclosure. |
| CT Lead | Respond to disclosure-related clarifications requested by the HA that must be addressed before the results are made public (if applicable). |
| CT Lead | Notify the Study Team Key Contact when the disclosure has been accepted. |
| CT Lead | Instruct the Study Team Key Contact to notify the Clinical Transparency department if the CSR is later reissued, requiring review and possible revisions to the disclosure. |
| CT Lead | Repeat the process for disclosing results on CT.gov and/or EudraCT/ EU CTIS, beginning with step V.K.1., if revisions were made to the CSR that affect the results that were submitted. |
| CT Lead | File documentation associated with the disclosure of results in the TMF. |

Results are disclosed in the form of a plain language summary (when permitted by local law or regulation) and an International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) Guideline for Industry (E3) ICH E3 CSR synopsis that is redacted according to industry accepted redacting principles. | Clinical trials conducted with products that receive initial HA approval: Redacted CSR synopsis publicly disclosed within 3 months after initial HA approval. / Clinical trials conducted with product formulations and indications that previously received regulatory approval:  Redacted CSR synopsis publicly disclosed within 12 months after trial completion. / Clinical trials conducted with products for which compound development has been terminated: Results are disclosed for completed trials within 12 months after compound development is terminated. Results are disclosed within 12 months after trial completion for trials that are ongoing at the time that compound development is terminated. / Timing for posting the plain language summary may occur after the redacted CSR synopsis is publicly disclosed. |

**Table 5 (attachments_table_5):**

| Activity | Description | Timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Results disclosed on the ClinicalTrials.gov website (CT.gov) | Summary results (consisting of a pre-defined data set) are posted for clinical trials that meet the definition of â€œapplicable clinical trialâ€ under the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act (FDAAA) 2007 legislation and 42 CFR Part 11 (Final Rule effective 18 January 2017). | Clinical trials conducted with products that receive initial US NDA approval: Results publicly disclosed no later than 30 days after US NDA/BLA approval. / Clinical trials conducted with product formulations and indications that previously received US NDA/BLA approval or compound development is terminated: Results publicly disclosed no later than 12 months after the primary completion date and until results have been submitted for all primary and secondary outcome measures and adverse events. / Results are also submitted for studies conducted with products for which the application seeking approval is withdrawn or FDA issues a letter ending the NDA/BLA review cycle without approval. / NOTE: An extension to the deadline for posting results on CT.gov may be granted when a written request is submitted that demonstrates good cause for the extension and provides an estimate of the date on which the results will be disclosed. Pending publication plans are not considered good cause for an extension. An extension may also be granted when an applicable clinical trial reaches its completion date before the product is approved for use or when the clinical trial investigates a new use of an FDA-approved product. Results are publicly disclosed no later than 2 years after a request for delayed disclosure is submitted. |

**Table 6 (attachments_table_6):**

| Activity | Description | Timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Results disclosed on EudraCT or EU CTIS | Summary results (consisting of a pre-defined data set or document upload and when required, a plain language summary) are submitted for clinical trials that are within scope according to the European Union (EU) clinical trial legislation. / Pediatric clinical trials conducted anywhere in the world (fulfilling article 45 and 46 of the Pediatric Regulation), conducted with products approved by the EMA, that may or may not be part of a Pediatric Investigational Plan as agreed with the EMA are required to be registered on EudraCT or EU CTIS. | Pediatric clinical trials: Results submitted no later than 6 months after trial completion in the EU or as defined in the protocol. / Adult clinical trials: Results submitted no later than 12 months after trial completion in the EU or as defined in the protocol. |
| Results disclosed on national (country-specific) databases | Results are disclosed on national databases when required by law or regulation. / NOTE: Astellas does not mandate disclosure of results for non-interventional, medical device or early access studies if there are no local/regional laws or regulations requiring such activity. | Timing is driven by country-specific requirements. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-2906 (1).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=54, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to outline the steps and process for the preparation, creation, coordination and sharing of Anonymized Clinical Trial Data with Researchers via the Clinical Study Data Request portal

- This work is mandated by Astellas POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information, Section IV.D.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-2906 (1).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: low (words=36, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in review and coordination of scientific community access of Astellas Clinical Trial Data.

- The following organization is in scope of this document:

- Data Science

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-2906 (1).docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List. Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document.

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Study Data Request (CSDR) Portal | A website that manages enquiries and research proposals for Astellas and other industry sponsors. |
| Clinical Trial Data Disclosure (CTDD) SharePoint site | An Astellas SharePoint site used by Data Science members to store documents related to CTDD activities. |
| Clinical Trial Disclosure (CTD) System | A web-based system to assist with clinical trial registration and result disclosure. |
| CSDR Form | A form within the CTD system that tracks data sharing status. |
| Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) | A document signed by the Researcher and Astellas after the Independent Review Panel (IRP) approves a research proposal. / Details can include a description of the proposal, contact information, publication and intellectual property provisions. |
| Data Sharing Coordinator (DSC) Mailbox | A shared Outlook mailbox used for sending/receiving emails related to data sharing activities accessible by appropriate Data Science representatives. This mailbox receives requests and enquires from the CSDR portal. |
| Enquiry | A question submitted through the CSDR portal concerning access to anonymized patient level data and/or supporting documents |
| Independent Review Panel (IRP) | A group of external experts that evaluates  a research proposal submitted to the CSDR portal. / The IRP charter is hosted within the CSDR Portal. |
| Research Proposal | A request submitted through the CSDR portal for information/data for a specific research topic. |
| Researcher | Person(s) requesting information/data related to a research proposal and/or enquiry. |
| SAS Multi-Sponsor Environment (SAS-MSE) | An environment hosted by the SAS Institute for sponsors to make their anonymized data available to researchers. |

---
