_Signals: medium (words=31, tables=1)_

- Requests for access to clinical trial data are entered in the publicly-available CSDR Portal by independent researchers.

- All research proposals and their final disposition status are archived in the CSDR Portal.

**Table 1 (process_research_proposals_from_the_csdr_portal_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |

| DSC | Check the CSDR Portal to ensure the IRP both evaluates the research proposal and documents the decision in the CSDR Portal. |

## SECTION 9: Anonymize Clinical Trial Data

_Slug: anonymize_clinical_trial_data_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-2906 (1).docx | docx | Section 9_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (anonymize_clinical_trial_data_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| DSC | After finalization of the DSA, identify the source data for each study in the approved research proposal |
| DSC | Create draft study-specific Data Anonymization (DA) metadata files for Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM)/Raw and/or Analysis Data Model (ADaM)/Derived datasets using the Astellas anonymization standards in the CSDR Portal. |
| DSC (Verifier) | Review the draft DA metadata files and provide feedback on DA rules to the DSC. |
| DSC | Update and finalize the DA metadata files based upon feedback received. |
| DSC | Run the DA process programs to create anonymized datasets (SDTM/Raw and ADaM/Derived). |
| DSC (Verifier) | Review the anonymized datasets and provide any comments to the DSC. |
| DSC | Repeat steps V.C.5 and V.C.6 until all comments are addressed. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=33, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for the development of disclosure documents for public disclosure of clinical study information or in support of scientific journal publications.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=110, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees involved in the development of disclosure documents required for public disclosure of clinical study information or in support of scientific journal publication.

- This SOP does not apply to the documents managed by SOP-1691 Subject Identifying Information Management.

- This SOP does not apply to the process of clinical trial registration and public disclosure of clinical trial results per SOP-1161 Process for Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information.

- The following organizations are in scope of the document:

- Clinical Operations

- Data Science

- Early Development

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Quality Assurance (QA)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Research

- Technology and Manufacturing

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List. Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document.

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Disclosure / Document | A disclosure document is any document created for public disclosure, including anonymized document (information permanently removed by masking/redacting or other anonymization techniques) or new document. |
| Protected Personal Data (PPD) Redaction | The type of redaction applied for masking protected personal data (also known as protected personal information (PPI)) in documents. For the technical specifications and definition of PPD, refer to STL-1938 Guide for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure. |
| Commercially Confidential Information (CCI) Redaction | The type of redaction applied for masking commercially confidential information (also known as confidential business information (CBI)) in documents. For the technical specifications and definition of CCI, refer to STL-1938. |
| Black Box Redaction | The type of redaction applied in some documents for masking protected personal data and/or commercially confidential information. For the technical specifications and definition of the black box redaction, refer to STL-1938. |
| Document Sanitization | Document sanitization for disclosure documents is defined as the process of ensuring that only the intended information can be accessed from a document. Document sanitization includes removing hidden information from document metadata that could pose a privacy risk. |

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=199, tables=0)_

- This document describes the global standard process.

- Disclosure documents are prepared according to the following principles:

- Anonymized disclosure documents are created using a final version of a document; no changes are made to the approved content apart from anonymization of the content.

- The anonymization methodology and the techniques chosen should confirm that the disclosure documents do not contain any data or information which can lead to the direct or indirect identification of any individual.

- The use of anonymization techniques is dependent on the document and context of the data published and includes:

- Methods based on the qualitative assessment by irreversible removal of values for variables which allow direct or indirect identification of an individual from the data, using a redaction tool

- Methods based on quantitative risk assessment, using a computer software

- The anonymization methodology and the techniques chosen for the preparation of marketing authorization application documents shall be documented in an Anonymization Report. When a development partner is involved, it is expected that Astellas procedures are followed when Astellas is directly responsible for public disclosure or clinical publication. A partner procedure may be used if agreed by the Asset Team / Core Medical Team (CMT) or equivalent, as appropriate.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Disclosure Document Lead | A designated individual (e.g., in Medical Writing (MW) Disclosure Document Lead, in RA Regulatory Study Team Member (RSTM) or equivalent role, or a Document Author for Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices / Agency (PMDA) disclosure submission documents responsible for oversight of disclosure document preparation |
| Contributing Reviewer | A functional representative responsible for reviewing disclosure documents. |
| Approver | An individual(s) responsible for approving disclosure documents. |
| Document Submitter | A designated individual (e.g., Clinical Transparency (CT) Lead, RA Representative, or MA Representative) responsible for submitting a request for the creation of a disclosure document. Confirms document(s) complete redaction process before public disclosure/inclusion in a scientific journal publication. |
| Document Team | A cross-functional team responsible for the creation and review of disclosure documents. Document Team includes Disclosure Document Lead, Lead Reviewer(s), and Contributing Reviewer(s) and Approver(s) as defined in Attachment 1. |
| Lead Reviewer | Provide expertise and support Contributing Reviewers to determine CCI. Act as primary adjudicator of disclosure document team or Quality Control (QC) comments. Lead Reviewer can also act as a Disclosure Document Lead. |

## SECTION 8: Prepare Documents in Support of Disclosure of Study Information or Study Results in Public Registries and Databases, or in Support of Scientific Journal Publications

_Slug: prepare_documents_in_support_of_disclosure_of_study_information_or_study_results_in_public_registries_and_databases_or_in_support_of_scientific_journal_publications_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=25, tables=1)_

- Some activities below may be performed in parallel, and some may be combined (e.g., review and approval steps) at the discretion of the Lead Reviewer(s).

**Table 1 (prepare_documents_in_support_of_disclosure_of_study_information_or_study_results_in_public_registries_and_databases_or_in_support_of_scientific_journal_publications_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Document Submitter | Identify the need for document(s) required for disclosure of clinical study information or scientific journal publication and an overall timeline. |
| Document Submitter | Submit a request for creation of the disclosure document to Disclosure Document Lead. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | Using the tables in Attachment 1, identify Document Team in collaboration with Asset Lead/Core Medical Team Lead (CMTL)/ Regional Project Representative (RPR) or designee. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Identify and propose PPD redactions in the disclosure document using STL-1938. Consult the E&C Data Privacy Office in case of ambiguities or if advice is needed to confirm the selection of effective anonymization techniques. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | In consultation with Lead Reviewer(s), identify CCI information along with the rationale/justification for redaction. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | If no PPD and CCI redactions are identified, proceed to run sanitization of the document files. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Distribute disclosure document(s) with proposed redactions applied to Document Team for review. Documents with no redactions identified are also distributed for review for the teamâ€™s confirmation. |
| Contributing Reviewer(s) | Review disclosure document(s) and provide feedback to the Disclosure Document Lead within the timeframe requested. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Reconcile comments/edits in consultation with the Lead Reviewer(s) and Document Submitter, follow-up on any comments/edits, and repeat review steps until all comments/edits are addressed. |
| QC Reviewer | Perform QC review to ensure document has been redacted according to STL-1938 Redaction Principles for Clinical Documents. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Address any QC review comments. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | If applicable, permanently apply final redactions according to STL-1938 and sanitize the document files. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Route disclosure document(s) for approval (refer to Attachment 1 for disclosure document approver roles by document type) and archive approved documents in the Electronic Document Management System (EDMS). |
| Disclosure Document Lead or designee | Notify the following that disclosure document(s) was approved: / Document Submitter / Document Team |

---

## SECTION 9: Prepare Documents for Publication of Marketing Authorization Application by Health Authority (HA)

_Slug: prepare_documents_for_publication_of_marketing_authorization_application_by_health_authority_ha_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-AST-10344.docx | docx | Section 9_

_Signals: medium (words=25, tables=1)_

- Some activities below may be performed in parallel, and some may be combined (e.g., review and approval steps) at the discretion of the Lead Reviewer(s).

**Table 1 (prepare_documents_for_publication_of_marketing_authorization_application_by_health_authority_ha_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Global Regulatory Lead (GRL) or designee (Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL)) | Identify the need for publication by HA of marketing authorization submission and an overall submission timeline. |
| GRL or designee (RRL) | Confirm the content of the submission (documents and modules in scope) for publication by HA. |
| GRL or designee (Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL)) | Submit a request for creation of disclosure (redacted and/or anonymized) documents to Disclosure Document Lead. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | Identify Document Team in collaboration with Asset Lead and GRL or RRL. Refer to Attachment 1. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or Designee | If applicable to the submission, prepare anonymized drafts by identifying proposed PPD anonymized content and anonymization report. Consult the E&C Data Privacy Office in case of ambiguities or if advice is needed to confirm the selection of effective anonymization techniques. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | In consultation with Lead Reviewer(s), identify CCI information and the rationale/justification for redaction. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | Distribute disclosure document(s) with proposed redactions applied to Document Team for review. Documents with no redactions identified are also distributed for review for the teamâ€™s confirmation. |
| Contributing Reviewer(s) | Review disclosure document(s) and provide feedback to the Disclosure Document Lead. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | In consultation with the Lead Reviewer(s), reconcile comments and/or edits, follow-up on any outstanding comments/edits, and repeat review steps until all are addressed. |
| QC Reviewer | Perform QC review to ensure document has been redacted according to STL-1938 Redaction Principles for Clinical Documents. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | Address QC review comments. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | If applicable to the submission, confirm CCI redactions are proposed for redaction in the anonymized disclosure drafts. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | If applicable, obtain document approvals prior to submission to HA. |
| GRL or designee (RRL) | Submit draft disclosure documents with the proposed redactions and rationale/justification to HA. |
| GRL or designee (RRL) | Upon receipt of HA review feedback, distribute it to Disclosure Document Lead and Document Team. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | If required, revise the draft disclosure documents and rationale/justification for acceptance or decline incorporating HA review comments. |
| GRL or designee (RRL) | If revisions were made, submit revised draft disclosure documents with rationale/justification to HA. Repeat Step 12-14 until agreement on the redacted content is reached between HA and Astellas. |
| Disclosure Document Lead | Confirm final QC review is performed. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or RRL for PMDA Submissions | Create final disclosure documents with redactions permanently applied, sanitize the document files, and distribute for final review to the Document Team for applicable submissions. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or RRL for PMDA Submissions | Obtain approvals of the final disclosure documents per Attachment 1 and notify the Document Team. |
| Disclosure Document Lead or RRL for PMDA Submissions | Archive final disclosure documents in EDMS or another designated archival repository. |
| GRL or designee (RRL) | Submit final disclosure documents to HA per SOP-1822 Develop and Submit Regulatory Submission Package. |

## SECTION 15: ATTACHMENTS

- Attachment 1

- Disclosure Document List by Review and Approval Roles

- The following principles apply to establishing Document Review teams:

- Information present in a document that may constitute CCI determines the members of a document team and level of review and approval required.

- The intent is that one reviewer per role will be included in the Document Team. These roles will work with the Disclosure Document Lead or designee during the creation of the disclosure document for disclosure of the clinical study information or publication by HA.

- At the discretion of Lead Reviewer(s) and Asset Lead, changes can be made to the Document Team â€“ additional reviewers and approvers can be included or removed from the Document Team. In particular, it is the responsibility of the Disclosure Document Lead (or designee) to identify and implement anonymization of PPD to confirm compliance with POL-412 Global Data Privacy Policy and this SOP. Disclosure Document Lead can request the review of the E&C Data Privacy Office, especially in cases of complex documents at the discretion of the Lead Reviewer and Asset Lead.

- A document team member may delegate responsibility within the functional area, when appropriate; however, accountability of the functional deliverable is not delegated.

- Local language documents/versions intended for disclosure should be drafted, reviewed, and approved by regional document team in consultation with the Asset team on CCI for global projects. The regional document team should be composed of those who understand the local language.

- When a development partner is involved, Asset Lead or designee (Development Project Management (DPM) Lead) will determine the reviewers from the partner company.

- Review and approval are not required for documents already disclosed to the public unless required by HA or when redactions are no longer justified. As the product development advances, information that initially was considered confidential may no longer be considered confidential at the time the first marketing authorization submission is published. CCI redactions applied for the first submission (study registry or study results disclosure) may no longer be justified for publication of the marketing authorization submission.

- Other documents not listed below may be prepared for disclosure (disclosure versions) as requested, and reviewers/approvers determined based on the document content (e.g., cover letter, other product-specific documents).

- Instructions:

- The Clinical Transparency (CT) Lead must pre-populate Supportive Tool (STL) with Protocol ID Number (including Header), and details, Section 1 and Section 2 (non-highlighted columns) showing the assessment of registration requirements for the study using known requirements for the country/ies selected to participate in the study. ClinicalTrials.gov should be listed if study requires registration per Astellas POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information or if Study Team requested registration even if United States is not a participating country. If there are no countries with applicable registration requirements, Section 2 must be completed and the Not Applicable box must be checked in Section 1.

- The Study Team Key Contact and the CT Lead must sign this form no later than 30 days prior to planned First Subject First Visit (FSFV) / Start of Data Collection (if final protocol is available) or within 7 days of protocol finalization (if within 30 days of planned FSFV / Start of Data Collection) to acknowledge the registration assessment and requirements responsibilities.

- If there are any requirements listed in Section 1 the CT Lead should confirm with the Study Team Key Contact the requirements have been completed and the information (e.g., submission or approval dates) supporting required registrations has been provided to the CT Lead (e.g., Section 1 Date columns completed / filled in). Registration Completion Acknowledgement should be signed as soon as all requirements in Section 1 are completed, even if prior to end of enrollment, and no later than 30 days after end of enrollment {e.g., Last Subject In (LSI) / Last Subject First Visit (LSFV) / End of Data Collection}.

- If Study Team Key Contact changes before all requirements have been completed, new signatures must be obtained using the Registration Assessment and Responsibilities Acknowledgement section of STL.

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=62, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define the process for the development, review and approval of all publications generated by an Astellas employee or

- non-employee as an author, and/or based on Astellas-sponsored research and/or related to Astellas products, therapeutic areas and/or business as specified in the scope below. This SOP is in alignment with POL-168 Global Publication Policy.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: high (words=695, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in the development, review and approval of all publications and associated supplemental materials (e.g., publication enhancements) in any language generated by an Astellas employee or non-employee as an author and/or based on Astellas-sponsored research (e.g., non-clinical, clinical (interventional and non-interventional studies), health economics and outcomes research) to be submitted for publication to a peer reviewed scientific journal or congress.

- This SOP also applies to:

- Publications based on Collaborative Research (CR) (see POL-AST-8264 Medical Affairs Collaborative Research Global Policy).

- Publications related to Astellas Primary Focus / Therapeutic Area (PF/TA) topics or business of Astellas-related topics with Astellas employees or non-employees as an author.

- Externally developed independent articles (e.g., invited reviews) where Astellas company review is being requested.

- Functional Units in scope for this SOP include, but are not limited to:

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- Primary Focus Development Divisions (PFDDs)

- Early Development

- Patient Centricity

- Market Access

- Rx+

- Data Science (DS)

- Clinical Operations

- Development Project Management (DPM)

- Regulatory Affairs (RA)

- Pharmacovigilance (PV)

- Legal, including Intellectual Property Development & Commercial (IP DC)

- Divisions under the Chief Scientific Officer (CScO) including Development Project Management (DPM)

- Divisions under the Chief Manufacturing Officer (CMfgO) including Development Project Management (DPM)

- For Alliance products, where Astellas has a co-research, co-development, co-commercialization, co-promotion, or collaboration agreement, Astellas endeavors to agree with the other company(ies) or party(ies) on the general preconditions pertaining to the publication process (i.e., alignment on a publication plan, and right to review publications led by the Alliance partner) to be governed by a publication clause in the Alliance Agreement or a mutually agreeable Inter-Company Publication Charter. Individual publications will be under publication process governance from the company who leads the publication. For all Astellas-led publications, all steps defined in this SOP on requirements pertaining to the development and approval of individual publications must be implemented in full.

- Astellas operates in many different countries and this SOP establishes a global minimum standard for conducting publication activities worldwide. Where an Astellas company operates in a country with an applicable local law, rule, regulation, Code or Guideline that sets a higher standard than this SOP, the Astellas company must comply with the higher local standard.

- This SOP is not applicable to publications derived from

- Material Transfer Agreement (MTA)-based research

- SOP-752 Investigator Initiated Trials for Compounds in Development

- SOP-714 Medical Affairs Grants for Research (Investigator Sponsored Research (ISR)

- SOP-1943 Medical Affairs Sponsorships for Research

- SOP-3050 Medical Affairs Led HCP to HCP Educational Activity

- SOP-1945 Medical Affairs Grants for Education

- Corporate Communications (e.g., press releases, investor communications)

- POL-392 Global Policy for Creation, Review, and Approval of Materials

- white papers

- open and closed symposia

- SOP-3061 Review and Approval of Medical Affairs Materials

- publications designated as promotional materials (e.g., publications based on market research results, commercial sponsored consensus statements or Astellas-sponsored journal supplements). Those publications must be reviewed and approved according to applicable local policies and procedures on promotional review.

- research results disclosure on public websites for registered trials as per POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information.

- As defined in POL-AST-8437 Global Policy on Enhancing Astellas Stakeholder Engagement (EASE) and POL-168, colleagues whose job / roles are primarily to support sales, marketing, or other strategic commercial activities may not influence content development, review, or approval for biomedical publications. Therefore, Marketing/Brand Leads may not serve as reviewers or approvers of publications. However, Marketing/Brand Leads may provide strategic insights on information needs and target audience for publication planning purposes, as well as planned use of publications.

- When HEOR resources are unavailable, local Market Access teams can be involved in data generation and associated scientific publication planning activities for non-product related epidemiology, disease-state, or economic evidence.  Market Access may also serve as authors on a publication where International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) criteria are met.

- Any publications based on Market Access-led evidence generation and targeted to peer-reviewed journals or international/regional congresses must adhere to this SOP and be led by the Scientific Publication team. For any market access led publication targeted to a local (single country) congress, Market Access is accountable to ensure adherence to necessary standards when Scientific Publication team support is not available.

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List. Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document.

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Astellas sponsored study/research | A research project (including clinical trials) where Astellas is the Sponsor and takes responsibility for the initiation, management, and/or financing. |
| Candidate-Nomination (CN) | The decision point when an asset has demonstrated sufficient confidence in the therapeutic hypothesis, modality, and potential value to justify investment towards Investigational New Drug (IND) applications; particularly investment in drug substance to support IND enabling studies. (See POL-996 CN Declaration Committee Policy) |
| Clinical Publication | A publication that is based on data generated from Astellas-sponsored research in humans or using human materials and/or data, including but not limited to translational science studies, Phase 1-4 clinical trials, non-interventional studies (e.g., non-interventional post-authorization safety studies), pharmacokinetic analyses, post hoc and meta-analyses, database analyses of health outcomes, other types of Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR), or registry data. |
| Encore Publication | A repeated presentation of data at different congresses to reach different audiences (provided allowable by the congress and that copyright requirements are respected). An encore presentation contains the same data as the original publication. An encore translation must utilize a certified translation of the original publication from a qualified/accredited translation agency/translator. |
| Non-Astellas Led Publication | Publication on Astellas products or TA of interest that have not been developed by Astellas such as publications developed by: / Alliance Partner, / Investigator-led publication from collaborative research, / Investigator who develops a publication based on Astellas-sponsored research, and / Independent publications (e.g., request for data accuracy check of an independent review article or invited external presentation on or related to an Astellas product). |
| Non-Clinical Publication | A publication that is based on data generated from Astellas-sponsored non-clinical research. |
| Publication | Manuscripts (e.g., primary, secondary, review article, letter to the editor), abstracts and presentations, that are made publicly accessible either through open access, journal subscription or meeting registration, and are generally subject to external review prior to being made publicly available. This typically includes peer-review for manuscripts and a review process for abstracts, which result in an invitation for presentation at a scientific or medical conference. Authors are selected according to the ICMJE criteria and any congress- or journal-specific guidance. / NOTE: Appropriate scientific rigor, quality, and ethical standards should be applied to all research targeted for publication to scientific journals/congresses. |
| Simple Publication | A publication that meets all of the following requirements: / Always authored by an Astellas employee or non-employee, and / Not based on Astellas-sponsored non-clinical or clinical research, including post hoc and meta-analyses. / Publication examples: / Astellas-related business topics. / Publications initiated prior to author joining Astellas. / General statistical methodology. / General pharmacology model, general pharmacometric modeling and simulation methodology. / Overview of best practices at a professional conference. |
| Translation of Publication | A non-English translation of an existing publication to be submitted to a non-English language congress or journal to reach different audiences (provided it is allowable by the congress/ journal and copyright requirements are respected).  Must utilize a certified translation of the original language publication from a qualified/accredited translation agency/translator. |

## SECTION 5: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-709 (1).docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Astellas Author | Astellas employee or non-employee who is an author as defined in the SOP. |
| Author(s) | Person(s) named on the byline of a publication and controls decisions regarding the publication, including but not limited to content, target journal or congress and order of names on the byline. All authors are responsible for disclosing financial or other potential conflicts of interest that might be perceived to bias their work, as required by the pertinent congress or journal. / NOTE: Pursuant to the ICMJE criteria, general supervision of the research group that is conducting or supervising a project is not sufficient for authorship. Similarly, participation solely in the acquisition of funding or collection of data does not justify authorship. |
| Department Head | Department-specific function head who conducts publication approval. |
| Designee | Officially and knowingly agrees to fulfill the roles and/or actions on behalf of someone else (e.g., of the designator). The designator is ultimately responsible for the roles and actions fulfilled by the designee. |
| Intellectual Property (IP) | A person(s) who conducts an IP review/approval and has knowledge of the intellectual property under review. |
| Lead Author | Directs content development of the publication and takes a lead role on behalf of the full author group. |
| Lead Statistician* | Ensures statistical methodology and data interpretation are consistent with the Astellas clinical study report or other Astellas reviewed analyses and summaries. Provides source data, figures, and analyses as needed. |
| Medical Writer | Provides publication writing support if agreed to by authors and under their guidance. |
| Presenter | A person who presents the content of the publication at a congress on behalf of the authors. |
| Publication Lead | An individual who is responsible for overseeing the development of a publication. (For English language publications, Scientific Publications personnel are publication leads. For non-English language publications, local affiliate or regional tactic owners are the publication leads.) |
| Reviewer | Assesses publication in the capacity of a Subject Matter Expert (SME). |
| Study/Activity Lead* | Medical Lead, medical monitor, or designee from protocol design and/or study team, or the HEOR lead from the protocol design team, or other Astellas personnel, leading an activity that results in data generation. |
|   |   |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=62, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to provide the actions to be followed for Investigator Initiated Trial(s) (IIT) for compounds in development. This constitutes all compounds which are unapproved/unauthorized in any of the three major global regulatory regions, i.e., Europe, Japan, or United States (EU/JP/US).

- IMPORTANT NOTE:	There is to be no soliciting of Investigator Initiated Trials by Astellas.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: low (words=70, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas employees and non-employees involved in the review and approval of IITs for compounds in development in relation to Astellas sponsored interventional and non-interventional studies.

- The following organizations are in scope of the document:

- Clinical Operations (CO)

- Development Project Management (DPM)

- Early Development (ED)

- Primary Focus Development Division (PFDD)

- Medical Affairs (MA)

- This SOP does not apply to Astellas company sponsored research or collaborative research.

---

_Slug: definitions_

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=254, tables=0)_

- An IIT is defined as a clinical study conducted by any external institution, research group, cooperative study group or independent external investigator/physician.

- In 21CFR312, FDA defines a Sponsor-Investigator as an individual who both initiates and conducts an investigation, and under whose immediate direction the investigational medicinal product (IMP) is administered or dispensed. The term does not include any person other than an individual. The requirements applicable to a Sponsor-Investigator in this context include both those applicable to an Investigator and a Sponsor other than Astellas.

- In accordance with this definition, a single investigator/physician acts individually or on behalf of one of the groups mentioned above and is the documented sponsor of the study. A request may be made to Astellas to obtain the IMP (IMP only) or may include a request for the IMP and funding in order to conduct the clinical study. Please note, budget should be evaluated according to local/regional fair market value.  Therefore, an IIT is an Investigator-sponsored study with a regulated product (in this case investigational, unapproved and unmarketed) for which the Investigator acts as a Sponsor-Investigator.

- An IIT request may be received at any point during the development phase of a compound prior to regulatory agency (-ies) first approval, i.e., preclinical up to phase 3 development. Following regulatory approval of a compound, the Asset Team  will determine feasibility and risk associated with transitioning the IIT to MA and/or providing support, as applicable.

- The request for an IIT must be formally submitted in a written format to the Asset Lead.

## SECTION 7: Receive and Initiate the Review Process for the Investigator Initiated Trial Proposal

_Slug: receive_and_initiate_the_review_process_for_the_investigator_initiated_trial_proposal_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=11, tables=1)_

- Perform the following steps upon receipt of a proposal for IIT:

**Table 1 (receive_and_initiate_the_review_process_for_the_investigator_initiated_trial_proposal_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Secure appropriate and sufficient information for team discussion from the Sponsor-Investigator and, if applicable, the Medical Science Liaison (MSL), i.e.: / Investigator name and institute / study properties {including objectives, target population or animal model / design (including outcome measures) / nature and quantity of involved Astellas product |
| Asset Lead | Ensure all requested material is reviewed by the Asset Team, and key applicable reviewers from: / Research / T&M Capability and Compliance / Intellectual Property (IP) / Relevant Head of PFDD / Regional representative of Head of Legal / Regional representative of Head of PV / Regional representative of Head of QA / Regional representative of Head of RA / Regional representative of Head of MA-Global |
| Asset Lead | Initiate discussion with the Asset Team. If the Asset Team decides to proceed, the following points, at a minimum, should be discussed with the appropriate PFDD Head and PFDD Medical Head for agreement; feasibility, safety, and alignment with strategy. Every effort should be made to align on a decision to decline or proceed within 30 days of formal review by the Asset Team. |
| Asset Lead | If the Asset Team declines the proposal, send a Decline Letter (STL-925 Astellas Development Investigator Initiated Trial Decline and Approval Letter Templates), to the requesting Sponsor-Investigator, copying the MSL, and store it in the applicable project archive. / NOTE:  This is a key step to be taken early in the process so that the proposing Sponsor-Investigator does not go through needless effort only to be declined. |
| Clinical Operations Lead (COL) or designee | If the Asset Team agrees to further review the proposal, provide a list of documents for the Sponsor- Investigator to complete (i.e., Sponsor-Investigator Document Completion Checklist for Investigator Initiated Trials, see Attachment 1). |
| COL / Asset Lead | Receive and review IIT proposal from Sponsor-Investigator with all required documents. Discuss the proposal with the Asset Team to make decision whether or not to proceed. / NOTE:  Asset Teams should consider the impact on other studies and overall strategy of the compound. |
| COL | If a decision is taken to decline the IIT following the due-diligence activities, send an IIT Decline Letter (STL-925) to the Sponsor-Investigator, copying the MSL, and store it in the applicable project archive. |
| COL | If a decision is taken to proceed, ensure the requested material is complete and routed to the Asset Team members, applicable PFDD Head and PFDD Medical Head. |
| COL | Ensure the Sponsor-Investigator has not been debarred (refer to SOP-1977 Exclusion and Debarment Screening SOP) and is not known to have been involved in criminal activity or under legal scrutiny (including any 483s from inspections). Obtain guidance from Legal if any additional due diligence is necessary. |
| COL | Complete STL-923 Astellas Development Investigator Initiated Trial Request Form. The STL-923 is used for internal reference and review process (see section V.B.) and is stored in the applicable project archive. |

---

## SECTION 8: Review the Investigator Initiated Trial Proposal

_Slug: review_the_investigator_initiated_trial_proposal_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (review_the_investigator_initiated_trial_proposal_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Evaluate the proposal within the Asset Team (Refer to Asset Team membership in Section V.A.4), including Chemistry, Manufacturing and Control (CMC) Development or Clinical Supply Chain (CSC) for material availability, for completeness and acceptance before requesting applicable PFDD Head and PFDD Medical Head review. / NOTE:  Astellas should not influence trial design {in alignment with SOP-714 Medical Affairs Grants for Research and POL-322 Medical Affairs External Funding for Research or Education}. Questions from the Asset Team review may be communicated back to the Sponsor-Investigator and the MSL. |
| Asset Lead | Facilitate review by the applicable PFDD Head, PFDD Medical Head, and key reviewers, including associated members as well as IP and Legal, to determine the completeness and acceptance of the proposal. / NOTE:  The costs and/or resource impact must be considered and should include CMC Development and CSC direct and indirect costs (e.g., IMP, including labeling) using existing Astellas methodologies for clinical development studies. |
| Asset Lead | Confirm and record feasibility and agreement of key reviewers via email and meeting minutes. / NOTE:  During the review of the proposed IIT, consider the following:  1) Can requested IMP be taken from existing batches without jeopardizing Astellasâ€™ in-house development activities and, if not; can budget and resources be made available for manufacturing additional IMP?  2) Will additional pre-clinical studies be required for the IIT to get Health Authority and/or Ethics Committee approval and, if so, can budget and resources be made available for these?  3) Consider impact of the obligatory disclosure of the study design and the impact of all possible outcomes of the study which will also be disclosed. |
| Asset Lead | Ensure from the key reviewersâ€™ point of view that the following are considered: / Pre- Proof of Concept (POC): compelling scientific and strategic rationale / Post- POC: is aligned with the overall strategy for the compound (as contained in the Core Medical Plan) and addresses unmet medical / scientific needs / Budget needs / Compound information / Phase of development / Collection of safety data provisions, including safety obligation to collect and report adverse events / Scientific merit / Legal review of the agreement / Patentability / Confirm costs are reasonable / Regulatory considerations / Agreement statement from all review groups |
| Asset Lead | Upon agreement by the relevant PFDD Head,  provide the following information to the Kachi Committee (KC) to request funding for the IIT: / Outline of the IIT protocol / Reason for accepting the IIT request from strategic perspective / Impact on the current Astellas plans and strategies (e.g., research, development, commercial, manufacturing, and regulatory) / Budget (e.g. IMP manufacturing, IMP supply, or including other indirect or direct cost within Astellas organizations outside development and/or if any new study is being proposed) / NOTE: KC endorsement is required even if only IMP is requested without monetary funding from Astellas. / NOTE:  KC may determine the necessity to escalate to the Executive Committee (EC). |
| Asset Lead | Obtain written decision of approval or decline from the KC. See Attachment 2, Investigator Initiated Trial Proposal Required Documentation Checklist to ensure decision of approval or decline is appropriately documented. |
| Asset Lead | Complete and send an IIT Approval Letter (STL-925) to the Sponsor-Investigator and copy the MSL. |

| --- | --- |
| Study Manager or designee | Track IIT planned milestones in applicable project repository. |
| Study Manager or designee | Obtain from Sponsor-Investigator and provide to the Asset Lead a periodic status report based on the contractual agreement, including, but not limited to: / IMP status (including reconciliation, return, destruction). / Recruitment and discontinuation status/report. / Safety reporting to Health Authorities/Ethical Committees and/or to Astellas (in alignment with SOP-714). / Reporting {including IND annual reports, Development Safety Update Reports (SUR), Annual Progress reports and other reports as appropriate}. / Raw Data (including but not limited to demographics, primary and secondary endpoints or variables, adverse events, serious adverse events, other exploratory data). / Publications (e.g., abstracts, posters, manuscripts, oral presentations). / Amendments to the protocol. / NOTE:  Each approved IIT must have database specifications developed and approved by Data Science. Reports of IIT should be disclosed according to POL-100 Global Policy on Public Disclosure of Clinical Trial Information. |
| Study Manager or designee | Assure closeout and destruction of materials as required per the terms of the contractual agreement. Document confirmation of destruction within the study file. |
| Study Manager or designee | Communicate results of IMP product review to the Sponsor-Investigator and copy the MSL. |
| Study Manager or designee | File Report or manuscript in EDMS. |

## SECTION 13: ATTACHMENTS

_Slug: attachments_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-752 (2).docx | docx | Section 13_

_Signals: high (words=486, tables=1)_

- Attachment 1

- Sponsor-Investigator Document Completion Checklist for Investigator Initiated Trials

- These documents include:

- Cover Letter (brief scientific question and hypothesis).

- Confidentiality Disclosure Agreement (executed by the Sponsor-Investigator and Astellas).

- Study Proposal/Protocol Synopsis (approx. 10-15 pages) including:

- Draft Protocol/Protocol Synopsis.

- Study title.

- Hypothesis/Scientific merit or rational (may or may not include preclinical work).

- Objectives.

- Background and significance of selected topic.

- Study design and Phase of development.

- Description of IMP including dosage strength and formulation.

- Duration of study.

- Statistical Analysis Plan (including sample size, justification, and power analysis).

- Experience and expertise of investigative team, appropriateness of research environment, capabilities of and background information about the study site(s) including safety reporting in case of treatment with investigational product.

- References such as papers or abstracts to support the study/rationale.

- Itemized budget, applicable to the study, and any additional outside funding and request for Astellas support.

- Estimated amount of IMP to be supplied by Astellas.

- Curriculum Vitae of Sponsor-Investigator having proposed the study or is responsible on behalf of the institution proposing the study dated less than two years prior to study start.

- Other reviewer interest or involvement in the study (e.g., government bodies, non-governmental organization, patient advocate group, etc.). Statement of competing or complimentary activity on the part of the Sponsor-Investigator with other pharma co-activity in relevant area, patents, biotech commitments, etc.

- The region of conduct by country.

- Documentation of the ethical commission and/or health authority approval for the study.

- Attachment 2

- Investigator Initiated Trial Proposal Required Documentation Checklist

- IIT proposal documentation should include but is not limited to the following:

- The IIT is the Sponsor-Investigatorâ€™s idea/initiative (i.e., has not been solicited by Astellas).

- Overall complementary Medical/Scientific Strategy for the product.

- Possible consequences on and/or dependency with the ongoing development projects, including scientific and data needs, in Astellas.

- Scientific merit and rigor of the study plan in proposed population or indication.

- Appropriateness in support of the internal clinical development plan, the regulatory strategy and proposed lifecycle management.

- Safety monitoring and reporting and management of toxicities, including any associated risks for subjects.

- Appropriateness and availability of budget and resource as indicated by the Sponsor-Investigator

- Estimated budget (i.e., Out of Pocket) and resource (i.e., required man hours) by each function (e.g., CMC Development, CSC, Research, Early Development, Clinical Operations, etc.) as anticipated by Astellas including IMP supply, packaging, labeling, and distribution.

- Availability of IMP and timetable for clinical supplies {blinded, placebo, comparators, etc., as well as the cost of goods and services (pack, label, store, ship)}.

- Currently available data (including preclinical in support of hypotheses and scientific question); studies in progress, provisions for data collection.

- Impact to active Astellas studies and confirmation that study is not duplicative of another Astellas-conducted study.

- Technical feasibility with respect to enrollment and timeline.

- Sponsor-Investigator and study site capabilities.

- Confirmation that the Sponsor-Investigator is not debarred or restricted from conducting clinical trials.

- Implications to regulatory status of Astellas project.

- IIT documents from the Sponsor-Investigator (see Attachment 1).

**Table 1 (attachments_table_1):**

| Attachment No. | Attachment Title |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Sponsor-Investigator Document Completion Checklist for Investigator Initiated Trials |
| 2 | Investigator Initiated Trial Proposal Required Documentation Checklist |

Q&A CTR: The documentation required to show compliance of the IMP and AxMP with GMP is outlined in Chapter IX and Annex 1 section F of the Clinical Trials Regulation: / â€¢ For IMPs authorised in the EU (even if not manufactured in the EU) no documentation is required. / â€¢ For IMPSs that are not authorised in the EU and do not have a marketing authorisation from a third country that is party to ICH, and are not manufactured in the EU, an authorisation referred to in article 61(1) and a QP declaration of GMP equivalence is required. In the latter case, if a Mutual recognition Agreement (MRA) covering also clinical trials is in place with the particular country, the latter declaration is not required if the MRA provides for GMP equivalence already. / â€¢ In all other cases, an authorisation according to article 61 of the Clinical trial Regulation) is required. Information regarding the GMP compliance of the active pharmaceutical ingredients is not required by the CTR (and can therefore not be required by the Member States Concerned.) |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1822.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=30, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the Regulatory Affairs (RA) process for developing and submitting a Regulatory Submission Package (RSP) to a Health Authority (HA).

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1822.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=119, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas RA employees and non-employees who are involved in the creation or submission of an RSP for which Astellas RA is responsible.

- This SOP also applies to Affiliate Quality Assurance (AQA) representatives who are responsible for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certification and site registration applications.

- The following submissions are not in scope of this SOP:

- Advertising & Promotion submissions

- GMP certification and site registration applications prepared and submitted in Japan or by a Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO). Note that for GMP certification and site registration applications partially prepared and submitted by a CMO and partially by Astellas, only the portion of the application prepared and submitted by Astellas is in scope of this SOP.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1822.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List. Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document.

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Content Plan (CP) | Complete list of documents for a specific RSP in which all documents have a unique identifier (e.g., document description/title, version, or date). / The format of the CP is to be decided by the Submission Content Owner in agreement with the Publishing and Submission (P&S) Lead. / NOTE:  A Submission Content Plan (SCP) is a CP which is created and available in Veeva Vault. |
| RA Owned Document | Any document intended to be included in an RSP which is either authored by RA (RA Owned RA Authored Document) or for which RA is accountable to confirm appropriateness of the document for inclusion in the RSP and RA is not the author (RA Owned non-RA Authored Document). |
| RSP | Any package (document or set of documents) created and submitted to a HA in paper or electronic format. |

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1822.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: high (words=331, tables=0)_

- This process is initiated when a Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) is informed that preparation of an RSP is required. This could be based on a variety of events, such as:

- Strategic company decisions

- Change in regulatory requirements

- Availability of new scientific information

- Outcome of CMC*- or CCTA- change control procedures

- Post Approval Commitments (PACs) and other marketing application follow-up measures*

- Periodic regulatory events

- Requests from regulatory authority (both during and outside of a regulatory procedure)

- Identified need for a GMP certification and site registration application. These applications are submitted in countries where it is a local requirement by HAs to approve sites involved in part or all of the manufacturing steps of a product intended to be placed on the market. Depending on the applicable local requirements, a GMP inspection of the site may be required as part of the procedure. Refer to SOP-3109 Inspection Readiness for more details.

- Administrative Changes

- RSPs have been categorized to provide clarity regarding roles and responsibilities for preparation of the RSPs which are in scope of this SOP.

- Refer to WPD-1023 Develop and Finalize Submission Content Plan and Regulatory Submission Package and WPD-1024 Develop and Finalize RA Owned Documents for additional details regarding Submission Content Plan preparation and RSP preparation.

- For Post-Marketing Surveillance RSPs in Japan, Medical Affairs (MA) is accountable for creating and populating the content of the RSP, and RA is responsible for submitting the RSP to the HA.  JP RA is responsible to collaborate with MA as necessary.

- For IND Annual Report (AR) and NDA AR RSPs in the US, refer to WPD-1062 Develop IND Annual Reports, WPD-1061 Develop NDA Annual Reports, or WPD-338 Develop and Submit DSURs in place of IND Annual Reports.

- For Periodic Safety Reports, refer to WPD-1082 Plan, Distribute, Submit, and Track Periodic Safety Reports.

- For PSMF related activities, refer to WPD-347 Contribute to PSMF Update and Submission of PSMF or Summary of PV System.

- * For CMC RA-related activities, refer to SOP-2556 Management of CMC RA Activities.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1822.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Global Regulatory Lead (GRL) | The GRL has global regulatory accountability for a compound/product.  The GRL is responsible to assess the global impact of any product development.Â  In regions where the RRL does not exist, the GRL is automatically also the RRL for that region. |
| P&S Lead | The P&S Lead has final accountability for publishing the RSP.  In some cases, such as when a local vendor or unique software is required, the RRL or RA Representative can take the role of the P&S Lead in agreement with the Global P&S Head. |
| Document Owner | The Document Owner provides overall document preparation oversight from a content and quality perspective and acts as primary adjudicator of comments. |
| RA Representative | The RA Representative is accountable for regulatory activities in a specific affiliate or country.  The RA Representative is responsible to keep the RRL informed of any developments regarding regional and global products.  The RA Representative can be assigned the accountabilities of the RRL in agreement with the RRL, RA Primary Focus (PF) Team Lead, and Regional Head. / For GMP certification and site registration applications, the role of the RA Representative may be fulfilled by an AQA representative. |
| RRL | The RRL is accountable for regulatory activities in the respective Astellas business region.  The RRL is responsible to keep the GRL informed of any development regarding global products.  The RRL can delegate the responsibilities to an RA Representative in agreement with the GRL, RA PF Team Lead, or Regional Head.  For the International and Greater China (INT-GCN) region, the RA INT/GCN Liaison or Product Manager (PM) may take the RRL responsibilities. |
| Submission Content Owner | The Submission Content Owner is responsible for defining the content of the RSP. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=29, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for interacting with Health Authorities (HAs) to ensure accurate and timely communications between Astellas and HAs.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=99, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to all Astellas Regulatory Affairs (RA) employees and non-employees who are involved in an interaction with an HA. This SOP applies to both development and life cycle phase products. This SOP applies to both communications initiated by Astellas to the HA and to communications in response to communications from the HA.

- This SOP does not apply to the following:

- Interactions with the HA that may occur in the context of an inspection. For such interactions, refer to SOP-687 Regulatory Inspection and Customer Audit Management.

- Interactions with the HA that are specific to Advertising and Promotion procedures.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: low (words=8, tables=0)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=151, tables=0)_

- HA interactions include any communication between RA employees and the HA, either in written or verbal format. These interactions may occur through a variety of formats, including, but not limited to:

- Verbal or written communications received from or sent to the HA (e.g., regulatory submission, request for information, HA meeting minutes, action letter) via phone/video calls, facsimile, email, or any other route of communication

- Meetings between Astellas and the HA (e.g., Scientific Advice, Investigational New Drug [IND]/New Drug Application [NDA] meetings, Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency [PMDA] consultation)

- HA interactions can take place at any step of the product life cycle.

- For regional procedures specific to the International + GCN (INT+GCN) region, refer to Attachment 1 INT+GCN Regional Requirements.

- For regional procedures specific to the European Union (EU)/European Economic Area (EEA), including safety-related questions received from an HA in the European Union (EU) region, refer to Attachment 2 EU/EEA Regional Requirements.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Global Regulatory Lead (GRL) | The GRL has global regulatory accountability for a compound/product. The GRL is responsible to assess the global impact of any product development. In regions where the Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) does not exist, the GRL is automatically also the RRL for that region. Conversely, if no GRL is assigned for a product, the RRL will take the GRL responsibility. |
| RA Representative | The RA Representative is accountable for activities in a specific affiliate or country. The RA Representative is responsible to keep the RRL informed of any developments regarding regional and global products. The RA Representative can be assigned the accountabilities of the RRL in agreement with the RRL, RA Primary Focus (PF) Team Lead, and Regional Head. |
| Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) | The RRL is accountable for regulatory activities in the respective Astellas business region. The RRL is responsible to keep the GRL informed of any development regarding global products. The RRL can delegate the responsibilities to an RA Representative in agreement with the GRL, RA PF Team Lead, or Regional Head. In case the RRL is not assigned {e.g., International and Greater China (INT-GCN)} RA INT/GCN Liaison or Product Manager (PM) will take the RRL responsibilities. |

| RA Representative | Facilitate the meeting with the HA. |

| RA Representative | Prepare and submit meeting minutes to the HA, as required, according to Procedure A. The draft meeting minutes may be submitted to the HA, when necessary. |
| RA Representative | Archive documentation, as necessary, per SOP-2528. |
| RA Representative | If communications are received during or after the HA meeting and need to be evaluated, refer to Procedure B. |

## SECTION 14: ATTACHMENTS

_Slug: attachments_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-1826.docx | docx | Section 14_

_Signals: high (words=406, tables=1)_

- Attachment 1

- INT+GCN Regional Requirements

- In the INT+GCN region, the RA Representative and the RRL collaborate to perform Section VI.A to Section VI.D as follows.

- Procedure A: Submit Communications to the HA

- For Action 4, the RA Representative and the RRL collaborate to perform the procedure.

- For archiving documentation in Action 8, the RA Representative performs the procedure in collaboration with the RRL, as necessary.

- Procedure B: Receive and Evaluate Communications from the HA

- For Action 4, the RA Representative and the RRL collaborate with the GRL for information sharing with appropriate internal stakeholders.

- For Action 7, the RA Representative performs the procedure in collaboration with the RRL, as necessary.

- Procedure C: Execute Actions in Response to HA Communications

- For Actions 2, 3, and 5, the RA Representative performs the procedure in collaboration with the RRL, as necessary.

- Procedure D: Plan and Conduct Meetings with the HAs

- For Actions 7, 11, and 13, the RA Representative performs the procedure in collaboration with the RRL, as necessary.

- Attachment 2

- EU/EEA Regional Requirements

- In the EU/EEA, the role of RA Representative is fulfilled by the RRL for all activities in this SOP in cases of interactions with the European Medicines Agency (EMA) or with the Reference Member State (RMS).

- Questions related to safety received from EEA Health Authorities are reported periodically to the EU-QPPV. Please refer to WPD-996 Perform Periodic Regulatory Compliance Checks in EST and INT & GCN Business Region and applicable instructions.

- Attachment 3

- Interactions with HAs pertaining to Clinical Trials

- Astellas may contract a CRO to act on Astellasâ€™ behalf for the purpose of submission of original Clinical Trial Applications (CTAs), amendments, DSURs, End-of-Trial (EoT) notifications and reports, correspondence, and/or response to HA comments.  In those cases, the following requirements apply:

- Ensure the CRO is informed to immediately forward any comments, requests for information, or other communication from the HA to the CTU, in order to allow for preparation of a response.  The CTU should then share the communication with the GRET (GRL, RRL, RA Representative) who will develop a communication and response strategy (refer to Section VI.C).

- An interaction with an HA can occur at any time during the planning, execution, or termination of the study.  While the CRO may be acting as Agent on Astellasâ€™ behalf, Astellas determines if the interaction should take place and who should be the primary representative for any HA interactions including meetings, notifications, clarifications, or any other circumstance.

**Table 1 (attachments_table_1):**

| Attachment No. | Attachment Title |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | INT+GCN Regional Requirements |
| 2 | EU/EEA Regional Requirements |
| 3 | Interactions with HAs pertaining to Clinical Trials |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WI-AST-14676.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=58, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Work Instruction (WI) is to describe the RA process for entering information into or updating the EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) and/or uploading document(s) for event notifications, including unexpected events, Urgent Safety Measures (USMs), serious breach, third country inspectorate inspections, temporary hold, early termination, global end of trial, and Clinical Study Reports (CSRs).

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WI-AST-14676.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: low (words=78, tables=0)_

- This WI applies to all Astellas RA, Clinical Operations, Early Development, Pharmacovigilance, Primary Focus Development Divisions, and Quality Assurance employees and non-employees who are involved in management of information in CTIS.

- This WI applies to Clinical Trials in the EU operating under the EU Clinical Trial Regulation (CTR) which are ongoing and already approved in CTIS.

- Clinical Trial milestone notifications are out of scope of this document.  Refer to SOP-1687 Submission of Clinical Study Documentation to Ethics Committees.

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WI-AST-14676.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: low (words=8, tables=0)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WI-AST-14676.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=100, tables=0)_

- The EU Clinical Trial Regulation (EU CTR) harmonizes processes for assessment and supervision of clinical trials in the EU through CTIS.

- CTIS provides functionality for:

- Sponsors to apply for clinical trial authorizations (CTAs) in up to 30 European countries with a single online application

- National regulators to collaboratively process CTAs in more than one country, request further information, authorize or refuse a trial, and oversee an authorized trial

- Facilitation of expansion of trials to other EEA countries

- Facilitation of transparency and access to information for any party interested in clinical trials conducted in the EEA through a searchable public website

---

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| SMT Co-chair | Responsible for identifying when a process triggers a requirement for an update to CTIS and to inform the RSTM. |
| RA Representative | The RA Representative is accountable for activities in a specific affiliate or country.  The RA Representative is responsible to keep the RRL informed of any developments regarding regional and global products.  The RA Representative can be assigned the accountabilities of the RRL in agreement with the GRL, the RRL, the RA Primary Focus (PF) Team Lead, and Regional Head. |
| RA Study Team Member (RSTM) | The RSTM is the RA member who has been assigned to represent RA in the study team and is responsible for the RA activities in the study team. / The role of the RSTM may be fulfilled by either the Clinical Trial Unit (CTU) Member or the GRL/RRL.  Refer to WI-AST-14598 Develop, Submit, and Maintain Clinical Trial Authorizations for RSTM assignment information. / The RSTM assigned to each study team is responsible for activities described in this WI. |
| Study Manager | The Study Manager is responsible for identifying when a process triggers a requirement for an update to CTIS and for informing the RSTM. |

| --- | --- |
| Study Manager/SMT-co-chair/QA | Identify instances which potentially require an update to CTIS and inform the RSTM.  Consult with the RSTM if clarification is required regarding what information triggers an update to CTIS.  Refer to WI-AST-14598, SOP-1687, SOP-1798 Plan and Implement a Safety Management Team, and SOP-2228 Implementing a CQA Project Oversight Strategy. |
| RSTM | Ensure disclosure versions of documents are available when required. |
| RSTM | Collaborate with the RRL, SMT, PRP, and/or Study Manager, as necessary, to ensure that CTIS is updated with applicable information. |
| RRL | For Clinical Trials included in a Marketing Authorization Applications in the EU (MAAs, line extensions, variations), ensure the redacted version of the Clinical Study Report (CSR), including applicable appendices, is uploaded to CTIS within 30 days of the European Commission decision or withdrawal. |
| RSTM | Notify the RRL, Study Manager, the Clinical Transparency Lead, and the Development QA representative, as applicable, that CTIS has been updated. |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WPD-1095 (1).docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=35, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Work Instruction (WI) is to describe roles and responsibilities and requirements to execute the process of Creation and Maintenance of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) components of Regulatory Submission Packages (RSPs).

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WPD-1095 (1).docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=179, tables=0)_

- This WI applies to Astellas Regulatory Affairs (RA) and Technology & Manufacturing (T&M) employees, Astellas subsidiaries, and non-employees who are involved in the creation and maintenance of the CMC components of RSPs during their lifecycle for which Astellas is responsible. This procedure can apply to documentation when collaborating with Development Partners as appropriate.

- The CMC components of RSPs are included in CMC background materials, Investigational New Drug (IND) Applications, Investigational Medicinal Products Dossiers (IMPDs), New Drug Applications (NDAs), Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs), Biologics License Applications (BLAs), the CMC portions of Normative Documents (NDs), and Astellas-owned  Master Files (MFs)*, and other documents containing CMC contents that are intended for submission to regulatory agencies.

- * In this document the term MF is used also for the equivalents Drug Master File (DMF), Active Substance Master File (ASMF), Biologics Master File (BMF), and dossier for Certificate of Suitability to the monographs of the European Pharmacopoeia (CEP) owned by Astellas.

- The following documents are out of scope of this WI:

- Japanese Module 1.2 Application Form written in Japanese

- Japanese Master File written in Japanese

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WPD-1095 (1).docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: low (words=8, tables=0)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL

_Slug: general_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WPD-1095 (1).docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=129, tables=0)_

- The CMC Components of RSP should be consistently created or updated to meet expectations with respect to standard content, format, and quality according to relevant regulations, guidance, and/or guidelines for pharmaceutical and/or combination products where medical devices and/or biologics are used as constituent parts of its combination products.

- This WI complements WPD-880 Expectations and Interactions Related to Development of Documents Intended for Submission or Disclosure with regards to the CMC-specific Submission Modules (e.g., Module 2.3 and Module 3). The principles to create RSPs are described in SOP-1822 Develop and Submit Regulatory Submission Package. The specific process for the CMC-specific Modules is described in SOP-2556 Management of CMC RA Activities.

- For contributions to Pharmacopeia Monographs for Astellas products, refer to MAN-404 How to Contribute to Pharmacopeia Monographs of Astellas Products.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: WPD-1095 (1).docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Contributing Author | Participates in development of CMC document, provides CMC part of deliverables as assigned, and ensures document complies with expectations according to CMC regulatory intelligence and functional scientific expertise. |
| Contributing Reviewer | Reviews document as assigned to ensure CMC components of RSP comply with expectations according to CMC regulatory intelligence and functional scientific expertise. Refer to Attachment 2. |
| Document Approver | An individual(s) responsible for approving the CMC document to signify scientific discipline review is complete, edits/comments have been addressed and the document/document component is ready for submission. |
| Document Team | Cross-functional team, established per SOP-1895 Development of Documents Intended for Submission or Disclosure, that can contribute to review the CMC components of RSP. |
| Global CMC Document Team | Cross-functional CMC team of contributing authors and reviewers, led by the CMC RA Scientific Lead (SL) and/or CMC RA Deputy, that develops CMC Components of RSP and ensures key messages are aligned with agreed upon strategy and planned timelines. Development Partners can be part of the Global CMC Document Team if necessary or relevant. / The members of the Global CMC Document Team can be reduced to SL (or deputy), contributing authors/reviewers, approvers, and relevant members where applicable (e.g., Astellas manufacturing plant, Affiliates) as listed in Attachments 1 and 2 and FORM-AST-32004 Global CMC Document Team: Roles by Document Type in case of: / updating CMC document as part of lifecycle / writing/updating of MF / writing/updating CMC portion of ND |
| CMC RA Scientific Lead (SL) | Provides overall CMC document preparation oversight from a content perspective. Leads CMC document content development, providing strategic input on scientific messages and structure of messages within the document. Acts as primary adjudicator of comments and ensures input and approval is received at appropriate levels depending on the situation. The SL for CMC documents is assigned from CMC RA. The SL has overall accountability but may delegate some activities to the CMC RA Deputy. The CMC RA SL may also author CMC content with support of the Contributing Author/SME. / For MF related submissions: / Except for Japan, the CMC RA SL acts on behalf of MF Holder and is responsible for the notification of relevant personnel that a MF submission is required and to provide input/feedback, as necessary, regarding the MF submission content. As to Japanese MF (corresponding to MF), Japan Domestic RA manages the MF. The CMC RA SL may work in collaboration with the MF Holder, Authorized Agent, CMC RA Deputy as necessary. |
| Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) | The RRL is accountable for regulatory activities in the respective Astellas business region. The RRL is responsible to keep the Global Regulatory Lead (GRL) informed of any development regarding the global products. The RRL can delegate the responsibilities to RA Representative in agreement with the GRL, RA Primary Focus (PF) Team Lead, or Regional Head. For the International and Greater China (INT-GCN) region, the RA INT/GCN Liaison or Product Manager (PM) may take the RRL responsibilities. |
| MF Holder | The MF Holder is responsible for the creation and maintenance of the MF. The MF Holder has final accountability for MF creation or maintenance submissions.  The MF holder of Astellas-owned MF is the legal entity of the manufacturer or manufacturing site of the active substance or the Marketing Authorization Holder. The CMC RA SL may act on behalf of the MF holder. |
| Authorized Agent | For MF-related submissions an Authorized Agent can be assigned in the country (or region) of submission and is accountable for the arranging the submission to the applicable Health Authority (HA) on behalf of the MF Holder. The Authorized Agent can be involved in the review and translation of MF documents and the preparation and translation of administrative documents in collaboration with the MF Holder and/or SL. The Authorized Agent is the intermediate between the HA and the MF holder. If applicable, the Authorized Agent is mentioned on the Letters of Access/Letters of Authorization (LOA) and Letters of Notification (LON). See Attachment 3 for more detail on fulfillment of the Authorized Agent role for specific Administrative documents. |

## SECTION 16: ATTACHMENTS
