- Attachment 1

- Principles of Global CMC Document Team: Roles by Document Type

- The following principles apply to establishing a Global CMC Document Team:

- The intent is that one person per role will be included in the Global CMC Document Team.  These roles will work with the Scientific Lead or the Deputy during the document development.

- Contributing Author is determined based on content of document and scientific specialty required. A Development Partner, if involved in document development, may fulfill some of the roles.

- Additional roles not listed in the table below may be included (but are not limited to) with the Scientific Lead approval.

- A Global CMC Document Team member may delegate responsibility within the function; however, accountability of the functional deliverable is not delegated.

- At the minimum, Scientific Lead/Deputy and Document Approvers are involved in the development and review of a stand-alone document amendment.

- The maintenance of the Authors/Reviewers list is conducted:

- For the development projects it may be in collaboration with Medical Writing.

- For maintenance projects by CMC RA.

- Documents not listed in FORM-AST-32004 should have Scientific Lead and Contributing Authors assigned as relevant to document content.

- The following principles apply to establishing Document Approvers:

- Documents not listed in FORM-AST-32004 should be approved by Scientific Lead and RA - Primary Focus Head (PFH) or equivalent as relevant to document content.

- The approvers of a stand-alone document amendment are determined based on the scope of the amendment. At the minimum, Scientific Lead approves an amendment.

- Detailed authors, reviewers, and approvers for document sections are described in FORM-AST-32004.

- Attachment 2

- CMC Documents: Contributing Reviewer Roles by Document Review Stage

- The following principles apply to establishing Global CMC document review teams. Also refer to WPD-880.

- Contributing Reviewers are assigned based on review stage of the document.  A Development Partner, if involved in development of documents, may fulfill some of the roles.

- Additional Contributing Reviewers not listed in the table below may be included (but not limited to) with the Scientific Lead approval:

- Contributing Reviewer may delegate responsibility within the function; however, accountability of the functional review is not delegated.

- *e.g., variations

- Attachment 3

- MF-related Administrative Documents Owned by Astellas: Roles and Responsibilities per Document Type

- Health Authorities (HA) require administrative documents are submitted as part of the MF submission package.

- Administrative MF documents to be included in original and maintenance submission types (e.g., amendment, annual report) vary by HA and should be determined by the CMC RA SL and/or Authorized Agent by referencing the appropriate Regulatory Agency Guidance(s). The Regulatory Agency Guidances provide information on the content and format (paper and/or electronic) of the administrative documents, along with address and/or fee details for the submission of the MF package. The website of the applicable HA should always be checked in order to see which forms / documents are needed.

- Table 2 lists the most common MF administrative documents and provides guidance on roles and responsibilities for preparation, review (if required) and sign-off where applicable. The documents can be prepared outside EDMS as templates to be used may vary country by country and may have to be downloaded from the HA website. The final submitted documents should be archived in EDMS.

- The table below provides an overview of the authorized agent role for the different countries/region.

- Table 1: Overview of authorized agent role per country/region

- *: including China, Taiwan, South Korea, Singapore, etc.

- Abbreviations used in the table on the next page:

- MF Letter of Access / Letter of Authorization (LOA)

- Some countries (like Canada) require a Letter of Access and others require a Letter of Authorization (like US). Both letters are referred to and abbreviated as LOA in this document.

- MF Letters of Notification (LON)

- A LON is required to be sent to the MF customer when a submission (any type) has been sent to a MF that supports their application

- Table 2: MF administrative documents (Note: the name of the documents listed below can be different per country)

- Attachment 4

- Guidance for Authoring and Reviewing of CMC part of Normative Document

- A Normative Document (ND) is used in the territories of Astellas Pharma Russia Affiliate (APRU) and in Ukraine.

- A ND is a Regulatory document which contains information on manufacturers, composition of product, specification, analytical methods, shelf life, storage condition and description of packaging of Product.

- Depending on the regulation in the applicable country, the ND serves as the approved regulatory document or as a supportive document to the approved CTD.

- A ND can be used by local regulatory authorities for quality control during local batch certification, during registration or during life cycle.

- A ND is based on the content of the European Common Technical Document (EU-CTD) and manufacturing and product related documents (e.g., technology transfer reports, analytical methods /analytical validation reports).

- For the submission to EAEU procedure, the applicable EAEU guidance should be taken into account.

- When the ND is used as reference for local testing, the ND should include the same level of detail as the source documents (i.e., analytical SOPs) of the involved plants.

- The RA representative of APRU or Ukraine is responsible for indicating if a ND is needed (or should be updated) for a product (to be) registered in one of the following countries:

- Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kirgyzstan, Moldova, Mongolia, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

- The Regulatory Representative of APRU is responsible for a correct translation of the content of the English version of the ND into the local language. It is not allowed to make changes in the local language of the ND without prior approval by both RRL and CMC RA, and without alignment of the applicable English version of the ND. Both the English version of the ND and the local language version should be archived in EDMS.

- CMC RA is in the lead for arranging the authoring / updating / reviewing of the CMC content of the English version ND.

- See Attachment 2 for an overview of the involved authors, reviewers, and approvers of the ND.

- Additional guidance for authoring / updating of the ND:

- Confirm with RA Representative of the relevant affiliate the regulatory requirements governing the ND per country (e.g., related substance to be mentioned in specification at the end of shelf life in Russia, reference to the applicable Pharmacopoeia and the need to mention the edition).

- Confirm with T&M the supply chain flow and which manufacturing related documents (e.g., analytical methods) should be used as source document

- Ensure alignment of the CMC content with the applicable CTD module and/or laboratory / manufacturing specific documents.

- Confirm with RA Representative of the relevant affiliate if during a renewal requirement the ND can be updated, i.e., changes and/or corrections can be included.

- In case of updating ND: confirm with Regulatory Representative of the relevant affiliate which version should be used.

- Guidance for reviewing of the ND:

- Confirm with reviewers which source documents have to be used.

- Agree with reviewers/approvers who should be involved on behalf of the Astellas and/or CMO (Contracting Manufacturing Organization) batch releasing site(s), and if applicable local QC site, and who will contact these sites/persons. Note: always involve CMOs in the review for new ND. For updates of existing ND: involvement of CMO on ad-hoc basis depending on the nature of change and/or the impact on the description of the performance of the analytical method.

- Check with agreed reviewers the Compliance with local requirements / regulations, consistency throughout the whole ND and consistency with the agree source documents and way of working.

- Table 3 provides an overview of the critical items for consideration when authoring or updating NDs, along with the responsible role.

- Table 3: Responsibilities and items that should carefully checked during review of the whole CMC content of English version of ND

- (*) information is included on request of HA and/or according to local requirements.

- I. PURPOSE
- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation
- and maintenance of standards for determining Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI)
- (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public disclosures (i.e., data
- and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the process for collecting,
- compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.
- II. SCOPE
- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to
- public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and
- the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas
- information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public
- disclosure of clinical study information (including product information for marketed and non-
- marketed products). This SOP does not apply to CCI for non-Astellas products.
- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.
- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide
- for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.
- The following organizations are in scope of this document:
- â€¢ Alliance Management
- â€¢ Clinical Operations
- â€¢ Communications & Investor Relations
- Printed/downloaded documents must be verified to ensure use of official current version.
- ASTELLAS CONFIDENTIAL AND PROPRIETARY Page 1 of 8

- VI. PROCEDURES
- A. Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure
- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is classified and disclosed in a consistent manner. Between
- Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-
- AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of
- existing CCI should be made when the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1
- to Phase 2 or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.
- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered
- CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-
- specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.
- Responsibility Action
- Public 1. Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734
- Disclosure CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review and approval of
- Lead FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library.
- Asset Lead or 2. Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI
- Delegate Public Disclosure Standards.
- NOTE: In GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards,
- for "Information that May Be Considered CCIâ€, consult
- with the Subject Matter Expert(s), Department Head
- and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on
- appropriate CCI classification.
- Asset Lead or 3. Document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-
- Delegate 35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team
- and/or other subject matter experts.
- Asset Lead or 4. Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-35734 CCI
- Delegate Asset-specific Library is final.
- Printed/downloaded documents must be verified to ensure use of official current version.

- I. PURPOSE
- The purpose of this Guideline (GL) is to describe Astellasâ€™ classification of data considered
- Company Confidential Information (CCI).
- II. SCOPE
- This GL applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to
- public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and
- the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This GL applies to Astellas
- information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure
- of clinical study information (including product information for marketed and non-marketed
- products). This GL does not apply to CCI for non-Astellas products.
- This GL is a companion document of SOP-AST-29658 Creation and Maintenance of CCI Public
- Disclosure Standards and Public Disclosure Tracking. Refer to the SOP Scope section for
- additional information related to scope.
- III. DEFINITIONS
- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.
- IV. CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS
- CCI standards apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-
- marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or
- after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval. Information relating to the nonclinical and
- clinical development of the asset is not, per se, commercially confidential.

## SECTION 3: public disclosure Project | Executive Summary

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_executive_summary_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: Public Disclosure Summary of Changes and Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 3_

_Signals: medium (words=249, tables=0)_

- Lack of centralized standards, oversight, and accountability for compliance with global regulations leads to inconsistent public disclosure.
- Public disclosure activities are decentralized and managed independently by M&D Functional Units
- There is no single point of contact or decision-maker responsible for developing cohesive standards/best practices and accountable for ensuring organizational compliance with global regulations
- There is no mechanism currently to centrally track what is disclosed in the public domain

- OBJECTIVE

- Ensure centralized standards, tracking and regulatory intelligence for public disclosure in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, industry guidance, as well as Astellas policies related to public disclosure in the public domain.

- 3

- If Astellas does not execute the project:
- Increased risk of inconsistency in public disclosures shared in public domain
- Potential exposure CCI impacting competitive edge
- Duplicative efforts by different divisions for identification of already disclosed information in public domains

- Start Date: March 2024
- Target End Date: Q4 FY24

- SCOPE OF WORK

- Develop a public disclosure strategy for data and document deliverables that includes the following components:
- Establish Astellas Global Public Disclosure Strategic Plan that includes public disclosure standards
- Centralize tracking of public disclosures shared in public domain
- Centralize disclosure regulatory intelligence/requirements (repository)
- Form a dedicated internal group that establishes Astellasâ€™ position on public disclosure and handles all deviations from standards
- NOTE: The scope will be limited to public disclosures pertaining to M&D. The scope may broaden in the future to encompass additional organizational groups within Astellas.

- PROBLEM STATEMENT

- RISKS

- TIMELINE

- Refer to Appendix â€“ Project Background for more details.

- Process Benchmarking & Internal Interviews (led by Data Science Team)

- 41 interviews conducted with various functional representatives
- Groups Interviewed:

- Approach

- Outputs

- Lack of public disclosure standards
- Lack of clarity of owner of the data and the decision maker
- Lack of visibility of public disclosure outside of Astellas
- Missing standard approach for collecting, monitoring and maintaining for Data Disclosure Regulatory Intelligence

- M&D LT Endorsement

- Identify and develop public disclosure strategy, standards and centralized activities
- To include maintenance of standards for phases of development (phase 0 â€“ 4)
- Centralization of public disclosure tracking outside of Astellas
- Centralization of tracking for public disclosure regulatory intelligence
- Establishment of a Public Disclosure Group (expansion of scope of current Clinical Transparency Group, that sits within Data Science)

- Inefficient engagement & Potential loss of credibility

- Inefficient use of time and resources

## SECTION 9: public disclosure Project | Business Value

_Slug: public_disclosure_project_business_value_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: Public Disclosure Summary of Changes and Background.pptx | pptx | Slide 9_

_Signals: medium (words=135, tables=0)_

- 9

- Consistency and Structure
- Public disclosure standards will establish a consistent framework for sharing information publicly throughout the drug development lifecycle for Astellas products, thereby reducing the risk of impacting our competitive edge.
- Enhanced Decision-making
- Clear guidelines on what constitutes CCI, empowering asset teams to make informed decisions about what can be shared publicly.
- Efficient Review Processes
- Using CCI Asset Library and the tracking tool as the resource to support decision-making will lead to remove duplication efforts in identification of already public information, reduced review time, reduced need for ad-hoc decisions and deviations from defined standards.
- Centralized and Supportive Infrastructure
- Establishment of the â€˜Public Disclosure Groupâ€™ will provide dedicated administrative support, allowing asset leads and teams to concentrate on sharing the required information needed to create robust CCI Asset-specific Libraries that reflect the defined standards.

- I. PURPOSE
- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to describe the process for creation
- and maintenance of standards for determining Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI)
- (herein referred to as public disclosure standards) applied to Astellas public disclosures (i.e., data
- and documents made publicly available). This SOP will also describe the process for collecting,
- compiling and tracking information on public disclosures.
- II. SCOPE
- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to
- public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and
- the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This SOP applies to Astellas
- information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public
- disclosure of clinical study information (including product information for marketed and non-
- marketed products). This SOP does not apply to CCI for non-Astellas products.
- The public domains in scope are listed in the OVERVIEW Section.
- Anonymization standards for documents for public disclosure are covered by STL-1938 Guide
- for Creating Redacted Documents for Public Disclosure.
- The following organizations are in scope of this document:
- â€¢ Alliance Management
- â€¢ Clinical Operations
- â€¢ Communications & Investor Relations
- Printed/downloaded documents must be verified to ensure use of official current version.
- ASTELLAS CONFIDENTIAL AND PROPRIETARY Page 1 of 8

- Role Responsibility
- Public Representative of the Public Disclosure team, who:
- Disclosure â€¢ Maintains GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards
- Lead
- â€¢ Facilitates drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI
- Asset-specific Library
- â€¢ Collects, organizes and reports public disclosures from applicable
- stakeholders
- â€¢ Serves as a point of escalation for asset/study teams to facilitate
- resolution of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library updates
- revisions as applicable.
- VI. PROCEDURES
- A. Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure
- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is classified and disclosed in a consistent manner. Between
- Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-
- AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of
- existing CCI should be made when the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1
- to Phase 2 or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.
- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered
- CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-
- specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.
- Responsibility Action
- Public 1. Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734
- Disclosure CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review and approval of
- Lead FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library.

- I. PURPOSE
- The purpose of this Guideline (GL) is to describe Astellasâ€™ classification of data considered
- Company Confidential Information (CCI).
- II. SCOPE
- This GL applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in or contribute to
- public disclosure standards and tracking of the public disclosure activities of clinical studies (and
- the products in these studies) as mandated by laws/regulations. This GL applies to Astellas
- information, data and/or documents that are made publicly available in support of public disclosure
- of clinical study information (including product information for marketed and non-marketed
- products). This GL does not apply to CCI for non-Astellas products.
- This GL is a companion document of SOP-AST-29658 Creation and Maintenance of CCI Public
- Disclosure Standards and Public Disclosure Tracking. Refer to the SOP Scope section for
- additional information related to scope.
- III. DEFINITIONS
- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.
- IV. CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS
- CCI standards apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-
- marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or
- after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval. Information relating to the nonclinical and
- clinical development of the asset is not, per se, commercially confidential.

_Signals: medium (words=244, tables=1)_

- Subject: [Dept] Request for Stakeholder REVIEW (Due date) â€“ NEW CCI Public Disclosure Standards Procedure

- Attach SH review excel

- CC: Functional SME

- Hello,

- As part of the Public Disclosure Project, a new procedure has been developed. This new procedure has been reviewed by functional subject matter experts (copied in this email) and we are now routing the documents for formal stakeholder review.

- As a recipient of this communication, you have been identified as a reviewer for your respective area. Your feedback is extremely valuable and we kindly ask that you support this review process by dedicating time in your calendar to review the document package or by identifying delegate reviewers to complete the review.

- Please review the below documents and provide us with your feedback, documented in the attached document comment form.  Feedback is due date EOD.

- *

- Keep in mind that final document formatting will take place once all stakeholder feedback has been received, so review and feedback related to format is not necessary.

- If no comments are received from you by the due date, we will consider it as your agreement that the documents are acceptable.

- Thank you in advance for your cooperation. For specific questions, please feel free to contact our team (by responding to this email) or contacting the project lead: Challoth (Shasha) Clarke (you can also copy your functional SME as well).

- Thank you!

- CPO Office Team on behalf of,

- Emily Bachman

- Challoth (Shasha) Clarke

- Sarah Snider

- Marta Nabielec

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=21, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI) (referred to as public disclosure standards)

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=178, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in public disclosure standards and public disclosure Astellas information data and documents that are

- ClinicaTrials.gov

- CTIS (EU CTR)

- EU Clinical Trials Register (EU Directive, via EudraCT)

- Japan jRCT

- National/country specificÂ registries

- Company website (e.g., Astellas Clinical Trials)

- Third-party website (e.g., TrialSummaries.com hosted by TrialScope)

- Scientific journal websites/databases

- Materials presented during scientific events and conferences

- HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (Non-interventional studies)

- Health Authorities clinical data public websites/databases

- Ad-hoc requests for Astellas documents submitted to EMA (Policy 0043)

- This SOP does not apply to corporate media/investor relations disclosures, shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

- This SOP does not apply to CCI for non-Astellas information.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Medical Affairs

- Pharmacovigilance

- Primary Focus Development Divisions

- Regulatory Affairs

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=20, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table below for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, textual) in any format/medium. |
|   |   |
| Disclosing Party | Astellas employees and non-employees who disclose information publicly. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing application modules, . |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information ( data and/or document(s))  public domain. |
| Public omain | The state of belonging or being available to the public, and not subject to copyright.  Refer to the OVERVIEW Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

---

## SECTION 5: OVERVIEW

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=149, tables=0)_

- Data and documents that are  by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following:

- Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released, could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. This procedure will be used to ensure the protection of CCI and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain.

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards will evolve and will be updated when necessary.

- FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, will be used as the basis for Asset-specific classification and described in this procedure.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Completes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. / Identifies revisions to FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when an Asset moves to a different development phase or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified. / Consults with Public Disclosure Lead to finalize FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
|   |   |
| Disclosing Party | Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Representative of the Public Disclosure team, who: / Maintains GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards / Facilitates drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library / Collects, organizes and reports public disclosures from applicable stakeholders / Serves as a point of escalation for asset/study teams to facilitate resolution of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library updates revisions as applicable. |

## SECTION 7: PROCEDURES

_Slug: procedures_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=106, tables=0)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is  in a consistent manner. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when

- the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 or

- when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified.

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

---

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or Delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that May Be Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert(s), Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | ocument Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-6011.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=35, tables=1)_

- CCI standards apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval.

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that  Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / Assay(s) conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special assay and assay methods: special test animal species or strains, assay methods, rationale for setting assay(s), etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc / Date of study period | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on common assay methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic assay(s) / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The assay methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of common solvents used in studies / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): treatment setting (e.g., in hospital), frequency of dosing (e.g., once daily, single dose), dosage administration (e.g., oral, IV). / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from Hs |   |
|   |   |
|   |   |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=45, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI) for the disclosure of Astellas information (documents and data) in the public domain (referred to as public disclosure standards), and to outline the process for tracking Astellas public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=217, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in public disclosure standards and public disclosure tracking processes. Astellas information (data and/or documents) that are subject to public disclosure standards and that are made publicly available under Astellasâ€™ development, or its license partners are found in the public domains included below, but are not limited to:

- ClinicaTrials.gov

- CTIS (EU CTR)

- EU Clinical Trials Register (EU Directive, via EudraCT)

- Japan jRCT

- National/country specificÂ registries

- Company website (e.g., Astellas Clinical Trials)

- Third-party website (e.g., TrialSummaries.com hosted by TrialScope)

- Scientific journal websites/databases/publications

- Materials presented during scientific events and conferences

- HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (Non-interventional studies)

- Health Authorities clinical data public websites/databases

- Health Technology Appraisal public websites

- Ad-hoc requests for Astellas documents submitted to EMA (Policy 0043)

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Market Access & Pricing

- Medical Affairs

- Pharmacovigilance

- Primary Focus Development Divisions

- Regulatory Affairs

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=19, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, textual) in any format/medium. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing authorization application (e.g. New Drug Applications, Biologics License Applications etc.) modules, or scientific publications. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (e.g., data and/or document(s)) in the public domain. |
| Public Domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public and may or may not be subject to copyright.  Refer to the Scope Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

---

## SECTION 5: OVERVIEW

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=153, tables=0)_

- Data and documents that are intended for public disclosure by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following:

- Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released, could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. This procedure will be used to ensure the protection of CCI and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain.

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards will evolve and will be updated when necessary.

- FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, will be used as the basis for Asset-specific classification and described in this procedure.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Completes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. / Identifies revisions to FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when an Asset moves to a different development phase or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified. / Consults with Public Disclosure Lead to finalize FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosure Document Coordinator | Any member of a function that is responsible for preparing documents for public disclosure. / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosing Party | Any member of a function that is responsible for facilitating disclosure of information publicly (i.e., party responsible for uploading/submitting/posting data and/or documents in the public domain). / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Representative of the Public Disclosure team, who: / Maintains GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards / Facilitates drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library / Collects, organizes and reports public disclosures from applicable stakeholders / Serves as a point of escalation for asset/study teams to facilitate resolution of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library revisions as applicable. |

---

## SECTION 7: PROCEDURES

_Slug: procedures_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=168, tables=0)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is determined and applied in a consistent manner when publicly disclosing asset related information. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when:

- the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 (refer to Section B Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when an Asset Moves to a Different Development Phase) or

- when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified e.g., when voluntary or involuntary information on the asset is disclosed (refer to Section C Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when Ad hoc Changes to Asset-specific CCIs are Identified).

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

---

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review, and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert(s), Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Review and document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

## SECTION 9: Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when an Asset Moves to a Different Development Phase

_Slug: updating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_when_an_asset_moves_to_a_different_development_phase_

| Public Disclosure Lead | Initiate review of existing FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library with Asset Lead or Delegate. / NOTE:  When the Asset moves to a different development phase, previous CCI classification may change. For example, the data is no longer classified as CCI. This should be reflected in FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. / NOTE: Ensure a check is done to verify what is currently available in the public domain as this information would not be considered confidential. |

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-6011.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: high (words=71, tables=4)_

- CCI standards in the table below apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval.

- The table below is a guideline which outlines both â€œInformation that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€ and â€œInformation Not Considered CCIâ€ for: CMC/Quality Related Information; Nonclinical Information; Clinical Related Information and Other Information.

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |

**Table 2 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_2):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: structures of metabolites and metabolic pathways in vivo and in biological matrices until NDA/BLA approval / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / Assay(s) conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special assay and assay methods: special test animal species or strains, assay methods, rationale for setting assay(s), etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Nonclinical study results: some nonclinical results during early development phases / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc / Date of study period | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on common assay methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic assay(s) / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The assay methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of common solvents used in studies / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |

**Table 3 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_3):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): treatment setting (e.g., in hospital), frequency of dosing (e.g., once daily, single dose), dosage administration (e.g., oral, IV). / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |

**Table 4 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_4):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Other Information | Other Information |
| Exposure data calculation / Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Product Cost / Product Net Pricing | Product List Pricing |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=45, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI) for the disclosure of Astellas information (documents and data) in the public domain (referred to as public disclosure standards), and to outline the process for tracking Astellas public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=217, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in public disclosure standards and public disclosure tracking processes. Astellas information (data and/or documents) that are subject to public disclosure standards and that are made publicly available under Astellasâ€™ development, or its license partners are found in the public domains included below, but are not limited to:

- ClinicaTrials.gov

- CTIS (EU CTR)

- EU Clinical Trials Register (EU Directive, via EudraCT)

- Japan jRCT

- National/country specificÂ registries

- Company website (e.g., Astellas Clinical Trials)

- Third-party website (e.g., TrialSummaries.com hosted by TrialScope)

- Scientific journal websites/databases/publications

- Materials presented during scientific events and conferences

- HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (Non-interventional studies)

- Health Authorities clinical data public websites/databases

- Health Technology Appraisal public websites

- Ad-hoc requests for Astellas documents submitted to EMA (Policy 0043)

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Market Access & Pricing

- Medical Affairs

- Pharmacovigilance

- Primary Focus Development Divisions

- Regulatory Affairs

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=19, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, textual) in any format/medium. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing authorization application (e.g. New Drug Applications, Biologics License Applications etc.) modules, or scientific publications. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (e.g., data and/or document(s)) in the public domain. |
| Public Domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public and may or may not be subject to copyright.  Refer to the Scope Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

---

## SECTION 5: OVERVIEW

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=153, tables=0)_

- Data and documents that are intended for public disclosure by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following:

- Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released, could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. This procedure will be used to ensure the protection of CCI and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain.

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards will evolve and will be updated when necessary.

- FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, will be used as the basis for Asset-specific classification and described in this procedure.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Completes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. / Identifies revisions to FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when an Asset moves to a different development phase or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified. / Consults with Public Disclosure Lead to finalize FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosure Document Coordinator | Any member of a function that is responsible for preparing documents for public disclosure. / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosing Party | Any member of a function that is responsible for facilitating disclosure of information publicly (i.e., party responsible for uploading/submitting/posting data and/or documents in the public domain). / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Representative of the Public Disclosure team, who: / Maintains GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards / Facilitates drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library / Collects, organizes and reports public disclosures from applicable stakeholders / Serves as a point of escalation for asset/study teams to facilitate resolution of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library revisions as applicable. |

---

## SECTION 7: PROCEDURES

_Slug: procedures_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=168, tables=0)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is determined and applied in a consistent manner when publicly disclosing asset related information. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when:

- the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 (refer to Section B Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when an Asset Moves to a Different Development Phase) or

- when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified e.g., when voluntary or involuntary information on the asset is disclosed (refer to Section C Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when Ad hoc Changes to Asset-specific CCIs are Identified).

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

---

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: 1. SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review, and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert(s), Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Review and document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

_Slug: updating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_when_an_asset_moves_to_a_different_development_phase_

For example, the data is no longer classified as CCI. This should be reflected in FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. / NOTE: Ensure a check is done to verify what is currently available in the public domain as this information would not be considered confidential. |
