## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: 2. GUIDE-AST-6011.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: high (words=71, tables=4)_

- CCI standards in the table below apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval.

- The table below is a guideline which outlines both â€œInformation that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€ and â€œInformation Not Considered CCIâ€ for: CMC/Quality Related Information; Nonclinical Information; Clinical Related Information and Other Information.

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |

**Table 2 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_2):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: structures of metabolites and metabolic pathways in vivo and in biological matrices until NDA/BLA approval / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / Assay(s) conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special assay and assay methods: special test animal species or strains, assay methods, rationale for setting assay(s), etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Nonclinical study results: some nonclinical results during early development phases / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc / Date of study period | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on common assay methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic assay(s) / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The assay methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of common solvents used in studies / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |

**Table 3 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_3):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): treatment setting (e.g., in hospital), frequency of dosing (e.g., once daily, single dose), dosage administration (e.g., oral, IV). / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |

**Table 4 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_4):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Other Information | Other Information |
| Exposure data calculation / Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Product Cost / Product Net Pricing | Product List Pricing |

## SECTION 5: CCI PUBLIC DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

_Slug: cci_public_disclosure_standards_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: GUIDE-AST-6011.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: high (words=71, tables=4)_

- CCI standards in the table below apply throughout all phases of development, from preclinical to Phase 1 to post-marketing Phase 4, and gradually decreasing as the asset moves into later stages of development or after receiving Marketing Authorization Approval.

- The table below is a guideline which outlines both â€œInformation that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€ and â€œInformation Not Considered CCIâ€ for: CMC/Quality Related Information; Nonclinical Information; Clinical Related Information and Other Information.

**Table 1 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_1):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| CMC/Quality Related Information | CMC/Quality Related Information |
| Drug Substance / Names and structure of active substance in early development stages / Quantitative composition for the active substance and excipients (formulated substances only) / Metabolites: Structural formula(s) of the active metabolite(s) and metabolic pathway(s) from which the manufacturing process of the active substance can be deduced and the disclosure of which could harm the legitimate interests of the company / Polymorphism, isomer, amino acid sequence, detailed information of study outcomes / Impurities: Descriptions of related substances and impurities, qualitative and quantitative information / Drug substance manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, amino acid sequence (new substances), cell clones to express protein/vector, impurities and degradants / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and active substances / Drug substance batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug substance manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc. / Drug Product / Quantitative composition for drug product (finished product) / Drug product formulation development (not marketed formulations) / Drug product clinical batches: e.g. dissolution profiles of tablets, details on dissolution methods / Company (In-house) developed cells and strains (when not in commercial is and not yet published) / Drug product manufacturing methods and processes: detailed information on manufacturing processes, characterization, pharm. development, validation, analytical methods, in-process controls, justification of specification, adventitious agents safety information/virus removal validation, Post-approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs) / Quantitative acceptance criteria for intermediates and drug product / Drug product batch size: production scale (commercial scale) / Drug product novel excipients information / Drug product manufacturers and suppliers: manufacturing sites, bulk manufacturers (except manufacturer of the biological active substance), excipients manufacturers, packaging site(s), batch control/testing site(s), details about facilities, partners/third parties such as suppliers, CMO, CROs, etc / Drug product packaging: technical specifications of the packaging such as color code, font, dimensions, etc. / AAV In Vivo Gene Therapy: / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / The name of a cell line or strain with genetic recombination, when in commercial use or already published (e.g., CHO cell, E. Coli K-12) / For biotechnology products, a general description of the active ingredient including the type 253 of molecule and its general structural features or of the type of producer cell / Information on the substances originating / from humans and other organisms (e.g., bovine foetus serum) / General information on the characterization of the active substance and statements confirming that the molecule is appropriately characterized / A general description of the type of test methods used and the appropriateness of the specification / Excipient names / Standard storage conditions, such as the storage temperature and period that are described in relevant guidelines / Units of the temperature, humidity and storage period in stability tests / Forms of the packaging / Conditions for creating deteriorated products, if published / Test condition and measurement value units for information on light deterioration or heat deterioration tests / Batch numbers / The fact that the synthesis or manufacturing procedure was changed* / The fact that the formulation was changed during the development program and the description of changes and bioequivalence tests * / Common purification procedures / Common techniques such as dissolution, mixing, filtration, etc. / Types and names of solvent, techniques if such information is published / *May be considered CCI for AAV In vivo therapies |

**Table 2 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_2):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Nonclinical Related Information | Nonclinical Related Information |
| Novel pharmaceutical concepts if not published / Novel mode of action if not published / Metabolites: structures of metabolites and metabolic pathways in vivo and in biological matrices until NDA/BLA approval / Innovative methods and/or study design if not published / Assay(s) conducted using a special substrate (created synthetically) and the name of the substrate / Special assay and assay methods: special test animal species or strains, assay methods, rationale for setting assay(s), etc. / Detailed information on analytical methods such as reagents, equipment, instruments, materials, etc. / Nonclinical study results: some nonclinical results during early development phases / Information on partners/third parties such as suppliers / Information on study sites: location, names of CROs and testing facilities, details about the facilities / Information on future development plans:  evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, etc / Date of study period | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Information on common assay methods / Commonly used techniques such as titration, ELISA and Biacore analysis / Techniques published in scientific publications and papers / Quantitation limits/lower limits and upper limits of pharmacokinetic and pharmacologic assay(s) / Drug concentration measurements / Information on labelling, such as labelling nuclide and labelled locus / The assay methods if the study is conducted using a standard dissolution study procedure / Numeric values if the dissolution study results have been published / The names of common solvents used in studies / Names of countries where nonclinical studies were conducted |

**Table 3 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_3):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Related Information | Clinical Related Information |
| Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): unit dose strength and strength of active substance, daily dose allowed, and maximum dose allowed for the medicinal product under investigation on justified grounds, i.e. when the specific information on the posology is not in the public domain and constitutes patentable matter, the disclosure of which before a patent application is filed (typically, after the completion of the trial and during the trial readout) would jeopardize its protection â€“ phase 1and phase 1/2 integrated trials / Biomarkers: new or novel methodologies not yet qualified (not disclosed in the public domain), including new methodologies to support future developments as regards secondary or exploratory endpoints / Innovative study designs and/or innovative analytical methods: company developed or modified assays and immunogenicity assays exclusively used by the company as the novel assays and not published / Information on critical reagents: not commonly used or not published / Information on validation of innovative analytical methods: innovative assays or assays and/or test methods modified or developed exclusively by the company or another third party and used exclusively by the company and not published / Study Endpoints and Results collected not supportive of the label: not supportive of a label (or future label claim) claim and not taken into consideration in the overall benefit/risk evaluation / Questionnaires, diaries, and other patient-facing materials provided by the third-party: written agreements between the sponsor and the third-party service provider expressly establish that patient facing documents (e.g. patient questionnaires) cannot be disclosed publicly | All other information is considered disclosable, including: / Dose related information about the drug product (study intervention): treatment setting (e.g., in hospital), frequency of dosing (e.g., once daily, single dose), dosage administration (e.g., oral, IV). / Information on study design and procedures / Rationale for the target patient population / Statistical techniques employed / Clinical study results / Information on the concurrent therapies / General information on PK/PD models, parameters, and the results of the PK/PD model simulations / Names of CROs and vendors involved in study conduct, duties and functions, including central laboratories, IVRS provider, image reading centers, conduct of assays / The fact that a consultation with HAs took place |
| Information on future development plans: evaluation of new formulation, innovative technology, or exploration of the effect of the medicinal product in new indications or populations, studies which are part of ongoing Pediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) / Information that may reveal strategic (contractual) agreements / Advice from Health Authority: detailed information about the scientific advice received from HAs |   |

**Table 4 (cci_public_disclosure_standards_table_4):**

| Information that MAY BE Considered CCI | Information Not Considered CCI |
| --- | --- |
| Other Information | Other Information |
| Exposure data calculation / Exposure data: patient exposure and sales volume by country / Projected exposure: projected post-authorization exposure data / Product Cost / Product Net Pricing | Product List Pricing |

## SECTION 2: PURPOSE

_Slug: purpose_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 2_

_Signals: low (words=45, tables=0)_

- The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to define Astellas Company Confidential Information (CCI) for the disclosure of Astellas information (documents and data) in the public domain (referred to as public disclosure standards), and to outline the process for tracking Astellas public disclosures.

---

## SECTION 3: SCOPE

_Slug: scope_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 3_

_Signals: medium (words=217, tables=0)_

- This SOP applies to Astellas employees and non-employees who are involved in public disclosure standards and public disclosure tracking processes. Astellas information (data and/or documents) that are subject to public disclosure standards and that are made publicly available under Astellasâ€™ development, or its license partners are found in the public domains included below, but are not limited to:

- ClinicaTrials.gov

- CTIS (EU CTR)

- EU Clinical Trials Register (EU Directive, via EudraCT)

- Japan jRCT

- National/country specificÂ registries

- Company website (e.g., Astellas Clinical Trials)

- Third-party website (e.g., TrialSummaries.com hosted by TrialScope)

- Scientific journal websites/databases/publications

- Materials presented during scientific events and conferences

- HMA-EMA Catalogue of RWD studies (Non-interventional studies)

- Health Authorities clinical data public websites/databases

- Health Technology Appraisal public websites

- Ad-hoc requests for Astellas documents submitted to EMA (Policy 0043)

- This SOP does not apply to corporate disclosures and/or media/investor relations disclosures, or information, data or documents shared with a third party or business partners under a relevant contractual or collaborative agreement. Refer to POL-1048 Disclosure Policy and POL-317 Global Policy on Third Party Lifecycle Management.

- The following organizations are in scope of this document:

- Alliance Management

- Clinical Operations

- Communications & Investor Relations

- Data Science

- Development Project Management

- Early Development

- Legal & Intellectual Property

- Market Access & Pricing

- Medical Affairs

- Pharmacovigilance

- Primary Focus Development Divisions

- Regulatory Affairs

- Research

- Technology & Manufacturing

---

## SECTION 4: DEFINITIONS

_Slug: definitions_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 4_

_Signals: medium (words=19, tables=1)_

- For definitions, refer to Enterprise Master Definition List.

- Please see table for definitions that are specific for this document:

**Table 1 (definitions_table_1):**

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Company Confidential Information (CCI) | In the context of this SOP and CCI included in public disclosures, CCI may refer to any non-public technical, scientific, business and other know-how and information, trade secrets, results and data of any type whatsoever in any media or format, including without limitation, ideas, discoveries, inventions, trade secrets, practices, manufacturing or analytical methods, tests, testing results, assays, techniques, specifications, processes, formulations, formulae, knowledge, know-how, skill, experience, materials, products and compositions, studies and procedures, drawings, plans, designs, diagrams, sketches, technology, databases, documentation or descriptions. Such data or information is also known as proprietary information. Confidential Information may also include intellectual property. / Any Confidential Information relating to the business activities of Astellas. This includes data or information that might be useful to competitors or that could be harmful to the company or others with whom Astellas does business if such data or information were disclosed, and includes data vital to the continued, successful operation of Astellas. |
| Data | A piece of information (e.g., numerical, textual) in any format/medium. |
| Document | Any document provided for public disclosure, including but not limited to: clinical study documents, marketing authorization application (e.g. New Drug Applications, Biologics License Applications etc.) modules, or scientific publications. |
| Public Disclosure | The act of sharing Astellas information (e.g., data and/or document(s)) in the public domain. |
| Public Domain | The state of belonging or being available to the public and may or may not be subject to copyright. Refer to the Scope Section for the list of public domains in scope. |

---

## SECTION 5: OVERVIEW

_Slug: overview_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 5_

_Signals: medium (words=153, tables=0)_

- Data and documents that are intended for public disclosure by study sponsors/applicants or Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH) can contain the following:

- Companyâ€™s information (company-related secrets and procedures) which, if released, could result in significant harm to the companyâ€™s competitive market position and financial loss and give a significant advantage to its competitors,

- and/or

- Study participants or study personnel personal information (PI; also known as protected personal data (PPD)).

- A companyâ€™s information classified as CCI, must not be released to the public. This procedure will be used to ensure the protection of CCI and consistency of Astellas public disclosures in the public domain.

- Standards Overview

- To allow consistent data classification, GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards was developed. Based on new information, approach, and/or requirements, CCI Public Disclosure Standards will evolve and will be updated when necessary.

- FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, will be used as the basis for Asset-specific classification and described in this procedure.

---

## SECTION 6: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

_Slug: roles_and_responsibilities_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 6_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (roles_and_responsibilities_table_1):**

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Asset Lead | Completes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. / Identifies revisions to FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when an Asset moves to a different development phase or when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified. / Consults with Public Disclosure Lead to finalize FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosure Document Coordinator | Any member of a function that is responsible for preparing documents for public disclosure. / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Disclosing Party | Any member of a function that is responsible for facilitating disclosure of information publicly (i.e., party responsible for uploading/submitting/posting data and/or documents in the public domain). / Utilizes FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library when disclosing information within the public domain. / Follows own applicable processes, as it relates to the material that is being disclosed. / Informs Asset Lead and Public Disclosure Lead in the event if CCI disclosure does not follow FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Representative of the Public Disclosure team, who: / Maintains GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards / Facilitates drafting, review and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library / Collects, organizes and reports public disclosures from applicable stakeholders / Serves as a point of escalation for asset/study teams to facilitate resolution of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library revisions as applicable. |

---

## SECTION 7: PROCEDURES

_Slug: procedures_

_Layout: Heading 1_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 7_

_Signals: medium (words=168, tables=0)_

- It is essential that Asset-specific CCI is determined and applied in a consistent manner when publicly disclosing asset related information. Between Candidate Nomination (CN) Declaration and Investigational New Drug (IND) milestones, FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library should be initiated and developed. Re-assessment of existing CCI should be made when:

- the Asset moves to a different development phase e.g., Phase 1 to Phase 2 (refer to Section B Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when an Asset Moves to a Different Development Phase) or

- when changes to Asset-specific CCIs are identified e.g., when voluntary or involuntary information on the asset is disclosed (refer to Section C Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when Ad hoc Changes to Asset-specific CCIs are Identified).

- The Asset Lead, in collaboration with the Asset Team, determines what information is considered CCI for the Asset. The Asset Lead is responsible for ensuring that FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is created and reviewed for the asset prior to each of the asset development phases.

---

## SECTION 8: Creating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure

_Slug: creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_

_Layout: Heading 2_

_Source: SOP-AST-29658.docx | docx | Section 8_

_Signals: medium (words=0, tables=1)_

**Table 1 (creating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_table_1):**

| Responsibility | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Consult with Asset Lead or delegate to initiate FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. Facilitate drafting, review, and approval of FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Identify Asset-specific data as CCI using GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards. / NOTE:  In GUIDE-AST-6011 CCI Public Disclosure Standards, for "Information that MAY BE Considered CCIâ€, consult with the Subject Matter Expert(s), Department Head and/or appropriate Legal department for guidance on appropriate CCI classification. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Review and document Asset-specific data in the Asset-specific FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library, in collaboration with Asset Team and/or other subject matter experts. |
| Asset Lead or Delegate | Inform the Public Disclosure Lead that the FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is final. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Archive the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. |
| Public Disclosure Lead | Inform the Disclosing Parties and Asset Lead that the final FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library is available for use. |

---

## SECTION 9: Updating a CCI Asset-specific Library for Public Disclosure when an Asset Moves to a Different Development Phase

_Slug: updating_a_cci_asset_specific_library_for_public_disclosure_when_an_asset_moves_to_a_different_development_phase_

For example, the data is no longer classified as CCI. This should be reflected in FORM-AST-35734 CCI Asset-specific Library. / NOTE:  Ensure a check is done to verify what is currently available in the public domain as this information would not be considered confidential. |

## SECTION 1: Connections Communications

_Slug: connections_communications_

_Layout: Document_

_Source: Connections Communications.docx | docx | Section 1_

_Signals: medium (words=215, tables=0)_

- Meet the New Public Disclosure Group

- Meet the New Public Disclosure Group

- Clarke, Challoth

- Head, Business & Operations Management, Public Disclosure

- Published 3/18/2025

- Do you know what Astellas information is considered confidential? Did you know it changes over time? Do you know what is and is not in the public domain?

- The Public Disclosure (PD) Group is your central point of contact for facilitating Company Confidential Information (CCI).

- Working with the Asset Leads and teams to help define an assetâ€™s CCI throughout its development lifecycle, the PD Group provides guidance on what constitutes CCI and a centralized tool to find Astellas public disclosures.

- Together, we clarify the confusion by identifying CCI for assets that previously led to inconsistent Astellas public disclosures.

- The end result is a dedicated infrastructure that is clear and transparent for everyone â€“ one that provides consistent framework for sharing information in the public domain and contributes steadily to Astellasâ€™ institutional knowledge.

- To support the PD groupâ€™s responsibilities, a quality document family has also been created:

- SOP-AST-29658:Â Creation and Maintenance of CCI Public Disclosure Standards and Public Disclosure Tracking

- GUIDE-AST-6011:Â CCI Public Disclosure Standards

- FORM-AST-35734:Â CCI Asset-specific Library

- Look for incoming training and tools about theÂ Public Disclosure GroupÂ as well as the above processes, roles and terms which comprise this function.
